title: Private 5G vs. Wi-Fi in the Enterprise: A Measurement Study of Tunability and QoE
abstract: Enterprise wireless is shifting from best-effort connectivity toward predictable, controllable, and flow-differentiated performance. Wi-Fi remains the dominant enterprise choice, while Private 5G (P5G) is gaining traction as an alternative with a richer set of operator-configurable knobs. Their practical value in real enterprise deployments, however, remains unclear. In this paper, we present a comparative measurement study of P5G and Wi-Fi on a commercial enterprise testbed, evaluating single-user performance, multi-user scaling, flow prioritization, and application QoE. Our results show the two technologies offer complementary strengths. Wi-Fi leads in single-user scenarios, but P5G's TDD configurability can match or exceed it in specific traffic directions. Under multi-user load, P5G's centralized scheduler delivers better fairness and stable latency. P5G's flow prioritization protects high-priority flows without starving background traffic, unlike Wi-Fi's winner-take-all flow priority model.
journal: Proceedings of the 20th ACM Workshop on Wireless Network Testbeds, Experimental evaluation & Characterization

title: ns3-GenAI: Integrating Large Language Models with ns3 for AI-Native Network Simulations
abstract: Existing ns3/AI bridges target numeric reinforcement learning (RL) pipelines and cannot handle the text-centric prompt/response exchange, structured output validation, and multi-node orchestration that large language models (LLMs) require. We introduce ns3-GenAI, an open framework that augments the ns3 shared-memory interface with three bridge-level features: a hybrid text-and-numeric memory layout, a fail-safe validation gate prior to writing back to the simulator, and multi-instance synchronization to support coordinated LLM workflows. These mechanisms provide a common, validated simulation path in which hosted and local LLMs, RL, and deep learning modules consume the same ns3 states and return decisions without changing simulator-side logic. We instantiate the framework in two complementary settings: a data-plane semantic codec and a control-plane self-organizing network (SON) agent. Across both case studies, hosted and local LLMs and conventional baselines occupy distinct quality–latency and throughput–fairness operating points. Rather than claiming a universally superior model class, these controlled comparisons demonstrate ns3-GenAI’s hybrid, fail-safe, and synchronized shared-memory path for evaluating generative and conventional network intelligence under identical simulation conditions.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 International Conference on ns-3

title: ns3-agent: Fostering Integrated Perception-Communication-Computing Research for Agentic AI Services via Cross-Platform Co-Simulations
abstract: The rapid proliferation of Generative AI (GenAI) has catalyzed the emergence of autonomous agentic AI services, spanning large language model (LLM) or vision-language model (VLM) based digital agents to vision-language-action (VLA) based embodied intelligence. Consequently, tokens and multimodal data streams have emerged as fundamentally new traffic modalities carried by modern wireless networks, actively reshaping next-generation evolutionary standards. Unlike conventional multimedia streaming, the end-to-end quality of experience of agentic AI services is governed by an intricate, bidirectional closed loop encompassing physical perception or request generation, wireless transmission, and edge inference computing. However, existing simulation platforms often treat network communication and generative intelligence as decoupled domains, failing to capture their dynamic, cross-layer interdependencies. To bridge this chasm, this paper introduces ns3-agent, a cross-platform co-simulation framework tailored for generic agentic AI workflows. By incorporating GenAI client environments, edge inference servers, and the ns-3 engine into a unified multi-tier architecture, ns3-agent orchestrates seamless cross-domain orchestration. To guarantee stringent temporal causality and high-performance data exchange, we implement a conservative time synchronization mechanism and shared-memory inter-process communication. Finally, we present a case study that couples a high-fidelity robotic physics engine with a live-deployed, operational Octo VLA foundation model over congested 802.11ax Wi-Fi environments. Simulation results reveal that wireless link quality severely degrades task-oriented performance metrics through complex temporal delays and semantic-transport layer coupling loops. Motivated by these observations, ns3-agent can serve as a reliable and foundational simulation sandbox to foster research in integrated perception-communication-computing for agentic AI services.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 International Conference on ns-3

title: Online Integration of NVIDIA Sionna RT into ns-3 via pybind11: Design, Features, and Validation
abstract: Accurate wireless channel modeling is fundamental to a realistic mobile network simulation. Current ns-3 spatial channel models, based on the stochastic 3GPP TR 38.901 framework, capture average propagation statistics well but cannot reproduce site-specific multipath phenomena, such as corner diffraction, street-canyon blockage, or deterministic line-of-sight geometry, which are critical for 5G/6G research and emerging digital-twin applications. This paper presents the design and implementation of an online integration of NVIDIA Sionna Ray Tracing (RT), a GPU-accelerated differentiable RT engine, into ns-3. The integration is realized through a lightweight pybind11 bridge that enables ns-3’s C++ event scheduler to invoke Sionna RT Python functions within the same process, avoiding the overhead of sockets, files, or external daemons. Channel matrices are updated dynamically at every mobility step, enabling closed-loop protocol simulations over physically realistic, geometry-based channels. We describe the architecture, the C++/Python API, and the setup procedure, and validate the integration through an urban mobility example that demonstrates coherent Doppler evolution and path-gain dynamics consistent with the simulated 3D scene. The complete implementation is publicly available in ns-3-dev master (through ns-3 merge request #2608).
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 International Conference on ns-3

title: Agentic AI at the Edge: Self-Explaining Autonomous Framework for IoT Incident Response
abstract: Incident response in Internet of Things (IoT) environments is difficult because devices are resource-constrained, visibility is limited, and remediation requires both contextual reasoning and explainable decisions. We present a fully local, autonomous incident-response framework for edge gateways. It combines a compact classifier that routes traffic by confidence, a tool-using language-model agent restricted to vetted mitigation actions, and an Explanation Engine grounded in the agent's recorded observations. Implemented with a 4-bit 3B model, the framework uses approximately 2.1,GB of memory and operates without cloud access. Evaluation on CIC IoT-DIAD 2024 shows that the detector achieves a weighted F1 score of 0.74 while limiting LLM-based triage to 30% of flows. The response agent selects appropriate mitigations in 92.4% of evaluated incidents, and its explanations achieve 0.99 faithfulness to the decision trace. These results demonstrate that autonomous, auditable IoT incident response is feasible within an edge-class resource budget.
journal: Proceedings of the 17th ACM Workshop on Wireless of the Students, by the Students, for the Students

title: Poster: VeriRAN: Explainable and Runtime-Verified Multi-Agent Control for Trustworthy AI-RAN
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-Native sixth-generation (6G) radio access networks (RANs) are expected to support increasingly dynamic control loops, where learning-based agents continuously adapt radio resources, slice priorities, and service behavior. However, this shift from static optimization to autonomous control raises a fundamental trust question: how can AI-driven RAN decisions remain safe when radio conditions change, telemetry becomes unreliable, or latency-critical services experience sudden stress? This paper presents VeriRAN, a lightweight runtime-verified AI-RAN control architecture that separates intelligence from authorization. Instead of treating AI agents as trusted actuators, VeriRAN uses them as intelligent action proposers that generate radio-aware and service-level-agreement (SLA)-aware decisions. Our verification shield is placed directly in the control path to approve, constrain, or replace unsafe actions before they affect the RAN.
journal: Proceedings of the 3rd ACM Workshop on Open and AI RAN

title: Real-Time RAN Observability at the Far Edge: AI on the Fronthaul
abstract: Operational RAN observability is reported every 5 to 15 minutes, averaging over as many as 1.8 million slots. Resolution is only half the problem: the quantities that explain a physical-layer fault, such as the beamforming weights the DU computed and the elements each layer actually drove, are not counted at all. Neither limit will cope with 6G integrated sensing, non-terrestrial networks, and ever-larger MIMO arrays. The 7.2x fronthaul split puts a standardized, tappable boundary in the middle of every modern base station; we argue it is the right place to obtain real-time observability, and that the analysis must run at the far edge, because the evidence is transient: it crosses the wire once, cannot be averaged down without losing the fault, and is not recoverable afterwards at any resolution. From passive captures, with no vendor-supplied instrumentation and no cooperation from either the DU or the radio supplier, we recover DU-side scheduling behavior and radio-side execution, including the per-beam and per-layer beamforming weights carried on the C-plane, separating measured quantities from those conditioned on an array hypothesis. On that extraction we ground an eleven-agent platform in which a language model only interprets measurements. Across three independent capture labs covering 4T4R, 32T32R, and 64T64R radios, a fourth lab read over the M-plane, and a dataset of 87 distinct captures, one unmodified code path recovered per-layer weights and revealed three faults nobody was looking for, two of them on the DU side, including a pair of effectively un-beamformed layers for which no alarm currently exists. A separate root-cause diagnosis was confirmed by the repair that followed.
journal: Proceedings of the 3rd ACM Workshop on Open and AI RAN

title: Physics-Informed Defenses against Poisoning Attacks on Learning-based Anomaly Detection in Industrial Control Systems
abstract: Process-based anomaly detection has been widely studied in industrial control systems (ICS) as a means to identify deviations from expected physical behavior. However, machine-learning-based detectors are vulnerable to poisoning attacks, in which malicious samples are injected into the training data, degrading detection performance, so that the detector misses alarms at test time. In this work, we propose physics-informed defenses against model poisoning in ICS anomaly detection. We leverage continuous physical process equations to identify inconsistencies between sensor measurements and the expected physical evolution of the system in order to build two complementary defenses: (1) residual-based filtering, removing physically inconsistent samples from the training data, and (2) physics-informed regularization, discouraging the learning of poisoned behaviors. We evaluate the proposed defenses on the SWaT testbed and show that incorporating physical process knowledge can mitigate poisoning attacks while preserving the detection performance of the underlying anomaly detector.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 8th Joint Workshop on CPS&IoT Security and Privacy

title: AutoTAG: A Testbed to Generate Automotive Attack Datasets
abstract: Autonomous driving is promising to revolutionize personal transportation. It relies on accurate sensor data and complex AI-based decision-making pipelines to perform safety-critical maneuvers, but recent research has demonstrated that these systems are vulnerable to adversarial sensor manipulations. However, prior work uses diverse testbeds or simplified simulation environments, making results difficult to reproduce, compare, and independently verify. In addition, prior work is often only evaluated on isolated modules or targets a single sensor type. Thus the impact of such attacks on downstream driving behavior or realistic multi-sensor fusion pipelines often remains unclear. Furthermore, attack datasets that could be used for training machine learning models or developing defense approaches are largely unavailable. Hence, there is a need for a framework that enables reproducible system-level attack evaluation while automatically generating labeled datasets. In this work, we propose AutoTAG, a framework that combines Carla and Autoware, an automotive environment simulator and an autonomous driving platform, to enable automated generation of datasets, including environmental sensor data and internal processing data of the autonomous vehicle. AutoTAG enables reproducible system-level evaluation of benign and attack scenarios and provides an interface to reproduce attacks from prior work. The resulting datasets include frame-wise attack ground-truth labels to allow easy use in machine learning applications, e.g., for attack detection training. We demonstrate the capabilities of AutoTAG with several different attacks, and provide the related datasets and artifacts.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 8th Joint Workshop on CPS&IoT Security and Privacy

title: Explanation Stability in IoT Intrusion Detection: A Comparative Study of SHAP and LIME Across Retrained Random Forest Models
abstract: The rapid growth of Internet of Things (IoT) deployments has increased the need for reliable intrusion detection in connected and safety-critical environments. Although machine learning-based intrusion detection systems can achieve strong predictive performance, their decision-making processes often remain opaque, limiting analysts' ability to interpret and trust model outputs. Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) methods, particularly SHapley Additive explanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME), address this limitation by providing feature-level explanations of model predictions. However, it remains unclear whether these explanations remain stable when intrusion detection models are periodically retrained, and prior work has not systematically examined explanation stability under controlled model retraining in an IoT intrusion detection setting. This study evaluates the stability of SHAP and LIME explanations for a Random Forest-based IoT intrusion detection model. The classifier was trained on the well-known datasets, CICIoT2023 and TON-IoT, and retrained six times using different random seeds while keeping the dataset, preprocessing pipeline, and train-test split fixed. Explanation stability was evaluated by comparing explanations across all pairs of retraining runs using feature-set, ranking, and vector-similarity measures. Across both CICIoT2023 and TON-IoT, SHAP produced substantially more consistent explanations than LIME, with more stable feature rankings and greater agreement in the most influential features across retraining runs. LIME showed greater sensitivity to retraining, producing more variable explanations even when the overall model behaviour remained broadly similar. These findings indicate that SHAP is better suited to system-level explanation consistency in retrained IoT intrusion detection models, while also highlighting that explanation stability alone does not guarantee correctness or operational trustworthiness. The results therefore suggest that stability evaluation should be incorporated into the deployment and validation of XAI methods for safety-critical intrusion detection systems.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 8th Joint Workshop on CPS&IoT Security and Privacy

title: Large language models linking traditional Chinese medicine knowledge and clinical practice
Approximative stochastic model for production risk assessment and batch completion time in manufacturing lines
abstract: This study developed an approximate analytical model for assessing production risks in manufacturing systems with sequential technological operations under uncertainty. While stochastic models allow detailed representation of production processes, their practical application is often limited by high computational complexity. To address this issue, an analytical approximation framework was proposed, enabling efficient evaluation of processing time under the influence of production risks. The model is based on a probabilistic interpretation of risk using a normal - ized risk priority index (WJRPN), which allows integrating the impact of 4M factors (Man, Machine, Material, Method) into the stochastic description of operation durations. Analytical expressions were derived for the expected value and variance of inter-operational delays, forming the basis for the pro-posed approximate model of batch processing time. A key advantage of this approach is a significant reduction in computational complexity com - pared to trajectory-based stochastic models while maintaining acceptable accuracy. Numerical results show that the relative error of the model does not exceed 5%, making it suitable for engineering applications. The developed model provides a practical tool for rapid analysis of production lines, enabling risk-aware planning, identification of critical operations, and improvement of manufacturing system reliability.
journal: Advances in Science and Technology Research Journal

title: Experimental strain evaluation and generative design optimization of a crane hook using finite element analysis
abstract: Crane hooks are safety-critical mechanical components used for lifting heavy loads, and their structural integrity directly affects operational reliability. The conventional crane hook designs based on analytical approaches may lead to conservative geometries with excessive material usage. This study investigated the generative design optimization of a crane hook modeled in accordance with the DIN 15401 standard. Experimental strain measurements were conducted at the critical cross-section of the hook under axial loading conditions. The measured strain responses were compared with finite element analysis results and used to improve the definition of the numerical material parameters. After establishing the finite element model, design constraints, preserved regions, obstacle regions, and boundary conditions were defined for the generative design process. The final optimized crane hook achieved an approximate weight reduction of 39.4% compared with the classical design while maintaining stresses below the material yield strength. The results show that experimental strain evaluation combined with finite element analysis can provide a useful basis for assessing and guiding generative design optimization of crane hook geometries.
journal: Advances in Science and Technology Research Journal

title: Adaptive hybrid FEA–PINN framework for fast melt-pool simulation in laser powder bed fusion of Inconel 718
abstract: Accurate prediction of melt-pool evolution is essential for optimizing Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) processes but remains computationally demanding when based solely on transient finite element analysis (FEA). This work presents an adaptive hybrid Finite Element Analysis–Physics-Informed Neural Network (FEA–PINN) framework for rapid prediction of the transient thermal field and phase evolution during LPBF of Inconel 718. A three-dimen - sional transient conduction model with an enthalpy-based phase-change formulation is first employed to generate high-fidelity thermal data using a moving Gaussian volumetric heat source. These data are subsequently used to train a physics-informed neural network that simultaneously satisfies the governing heat-transfer equation, initial and boundary conditions, and phase-transition constraints. An adaptive refinement strategy combines localized mesh refinement, residual-based collocation-point enrichment, and on-demand local FEA correction to improve prediction accuracy while limiting computational cost. For the investigated LPBF process (laser power 300 W, scan speed 1000 mm s⁻¹, layer thickness 40 μm, beam diameter 80 μm), the proposed framework predicts the tran - sient temperature field with a mean relative error of 1.48% compared with high-fidelity FEA. The corresponding errors in melt-pool width, depth, and length are 2.12%, 2.37%, and 2.41%, respectively, while the liquid-fraction prediction error remains below 2.1%. The predicted average melt-pool dimensions are approximately 128 μm (width), 67 μm (depth), and 245 μm (length), in agreement with reported experimental values for conduction-mode LPBF of Inconel 718. A conventional transient FEA simulation required approximately 27.4 h, whereas the trained hybrid FEA–PINN model completed the corresponding prediction in 15.8 min, representing a computational speedup of approximately 104× while preserving engineering-level accuracy. The proposed framework is applicable to conduction-mode LPBF, where evaporation, recoil pressure, keyhole formation, free-surface deformation, and individual powder-particle dynamics are neglected. The results demonstrate that adaptive FEA–PINN coupling provides an efficient surrogate for high-fidelity thermal simulations and offers a practical approach for rapid process optimization and digital-twin applications in metal additive manufacturing.

title: The Use of AI Agents in Small Businesses: Applications, Benefits, Challenges and an Adoption Framework
abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) form the backbone of most economies, yet they typically operate with limited staff, tight budgets and little specialist technical capacity. Recent advances in large language models have produced AI agents: software systems that can interpret goals, plan multi-step tasks, use external tools and act with a degree of autonomy. This paper examines how AI agents can be applied in small businesses, what benefits they may offer, and what risks must be managed. Drawing on the literature on intelligent agents, technology adoption and the resource-based view of the firm, the paper develops a function-by-function analysis covering customer service, sales and marketing, finance and administration, operations, and human resources. It then proposes a five-stage adoption framework and a set of research propositions tailored to the constraints of small firms. The analysis suggests that AI agents are most valuable when applied to repetitive, text-heavy and tool-mediated tasks, when the owner-manager remains in the loop for consequential decisions, and when data protection, transparency and vendor dependence are addressed from the outset. The paper concludes with practical guidance for owner-managers and directions for empirical research.

title: When Firms Delegate Tax Decisions to AI Agents: Costly Objective Correction and Executable Compliance Constraints
abstract: Tax enforcement can separate the party bearing liability from the system selecting the tax position. We study a firm that delegates reporting to an optimizer whose executable objective only partially incorporates expected sanctions. The owner bears all monetary liability and can correct the objective, but correction consumes resources. A quadratic benchmark delivers explicit reporting, specification and adoption rules. Greater capability can first increase and then eliminate concealment even when sanction pass-through is unchanged: stronger responses to a corrective mandate make endogenous correction more effective. Strict liability implements compliance above a calculable enforcement threshold, but the threshold can exceed that required for direct human choice and need not be feasible under bounded sanctions. Executable certification caps provide an alternative instrument. A cap can lower the default action yet increase concealment relative to an optimally corrected unrestricted system because the owner stops investing in correction. We characterize voluntary compliance certification and a welfare-maximizing cap within the binding-cap regime, accounting separately for lawful service losses, transfers and real costs. Private gates can remove the incremental value of certification. A shared-mandate extension identifies the highest-default contexts that govern complete compliance, while alternative control costs and action curvature show that the capability reversal and finite exact-compliance threshold are not general. The results describe a delegated-optimization friction rather than an intrinsic preference of AI systems, and they do not establish a universal advantage of certification. Numerical illustrations and curvature checks use normalized parameters, not empirical estimates.

title: A Novel Fuzzy Hybrid Deep Learning Architecture for Spatiotemporal PM2.5 Prediction
abstract: Accurate particulate matter with a diameter of 2.5 µm (PM 2.5 ) prediction is important for air-quality management and public-health protection. Since dense monitoring networks are costly and spatially limited, forecasting models are needed to complement station observations and estimate pollution conditions more broadly. This study develops a novel fuzzy transformer-convolutional neural network-gated recurrent unit (NFT-CNN-GRU) framework for one-day-ahead PM 2.5 forecasting in Tehran. The model integrates meteorological and satellite-derived time-series data with topographic, population, and road-network information collected during 2014–2016, using 2014–2015 for training and 2016 for independent testing. The proposed architecture introduces uncertainty-adaptive Gaussian fuzzification to better represent uncertain environmental observations, while CNN extracts local and spatial patterns and GRU models their temporal evolution. Transformer captures long-range dependencies, and an adaptive cross-branch attention mechanism dynamically integrates global contextual information with CNN-GRU spatiotemporal features. Finally, the fuzzy representation is combined with the learned deep features to produce the PM 2.5 forecast. The proposed NFT-CNN-GRU framework was compared with seven competing models and achieved the best performance, with a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.73 µg/m³, coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.95, and a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 0.28%. Both 1-km-resolution and station-based PM 2.5 prediction maps were generated, showing strong spatial agreement with observed pollution patterns. The framework also demonstrated high computational practicality, with an inference latency of 9.3 ms, a variance of only 0.037896 across 15 independent runs, rapid convergence, and statistically significant improvements over all benchmark models at α = 0.01. Feature-importance analysis further showed that aerosol optical depth (AOD), road-network density, weighted population, and normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) were among the most influential predictors of PM 2.5 variability. Their dominant contributions highlight the importance of combining atmospheric aerosol information with urban activity and land-surface characteristics for reliable pollution forecasting. These findings indicate that NFT-CNN-GRU provides an accurate, stable, and computationally feasible solution for operational PM 2.5 forecasting and spatial air-quality assessment.

title: Standard Curves of Productivity, Tree Row Volume, and Yield Efficiency by Tree Age of Commercial Sweet Orange Groves in the São Paulo Citrus Belt, Brazil
abstract: Brazil is the world’s largest producer and exporter of orange juice, with most production concentrated in São Paulo and southwestern Minas Gerais (the São Paulo citrus belt). Information on the agronomic performance of orange trees throughout the grove lifespan, including productivity and tree size, is essential for reliable assessments of production costs, revenue, and profitability. This study aimed to develop standard curves for productivity, tree row volume (TRV), and yield efficiency as a function of tree age and stratified by cultivar, region, and planting density. The analysis used data collected by the Orange Crop Forecast conducted by Fundecitrus in commercial sweet orange groves over nine consecutive seasons, from 2016–17 to 2024–25. Grove productivity increased up to ∼14 years of age and declined thereafter, with estimated yields of 25.0, 41.0, 45.1, and 37.1 t/ha for groves aged 5, 10, 15, and 20 years, respectively. ‘Hamlin’ cultivar, southwestern region, and groves planted at high density showed the highest productivity. TRV increased with grove age, reaching 14.1, 26.9, 34.8, and 37.8 thousand m³/ha at the reference ages noted above, with the highest volumes observed for ‘Hamlin’, northern and northwestern regions, and high-density groves. Yield efficiency declined with age, with 16.6, 13.3, 10.8, and 9.2 fruits/m³ at 5, 10, 15, and 20 years, respectively. ‘Natal’, southwestern region, and high-density groves were the strata that had the highest yield efficiency. These results provide a robust reference for evaluating grove performance over time and support economic feasibility analysis, management planning, and strategic decision-making in the citrus industry.

title: Determinants of Irrigation Innovation Adoption in Southern Italian Agriculture
abstract: The adoption of innovative irrigation technologies is strategic for improving water efficiency and strengthening the resilience of agricultural systems amid growing environmental, climatic, and economic pressures. This study examines the factors associated with the adoption of irrigation innovations among 201 FADN fruit and vegetable farms in Basilicata, Calabria, Campania, and Apulia, using a binary logistic regression model including structural, attitudinal, economic, and environmental variables. The results show that innovation orientation and perceived shortage of qualified staff are the factors most strongly associated with adoption. The former supports the relevance of behavioral and attitudinal factors in technological investment decisions; the latter may reflect the substitution of scarce specialized labor with technology, although reverse causality cannot be ruled out. Perceived high water costs are also significantly associated with a greater propensity for adoption. Larger farms (over 14 hectares) show a higher likelihood of adoption, despite perceiving financial constraints more acutely. Environmental concern and perceived water scarcity show only marginally significant positive associations (p < 0.10), while organic status and perceived lack of financial support show no significant association, nor do the socio-demographic control variables. Overall, irrigation innovation adoption is associated with individual, structural, economic, and organizational factors, offering insights into policies promoting efficient irrigation in similar Mediterranean farming contexts.

title: Mask-Guided Diffusion-Consistency Network for Multimodal Hyperspectral Point-Cloud Mineral Mapping
abstract: Multimodal hyperspectral point-cloud mineral mapping is complicated by spectral ambiguity and uneven class distributions. Graph encoders integrate complementary observations, but feature aggregation does not necessarily yield spatially consistent class probabilities. We introduce a Mask-Guided Diffusion-Consistency Network combining multimodal graph encoding, conditional semantic-mask denoising and k-nearest-neighbour probability refinement. Noise-prediction and mask-reconstruction supervision regularize semantic estimates, while neighbourhood propagation encourages spatial continuity. The components are jointly trained with base and refined classification losses and perturbation consistency. Across five independent training runs on Tinto, the model achieves 80.93±0.31% overall accuracy, compared with 74.99±0.54% for a matched-budget backbone (mean ± sample standard deviation). The difference between means is 5.94 percentage points; the 10.46-point difference from the original backbone also includes continued-training gains. Five-run class-wise results reveal lower mean recall for Mafic B and Felsic B despite improved aggregate accuracy. Existing single-run ablations favour the complete model, but the 0.02-point validation fusion margin does not establish a meaningful direct diffusion effect. VNIR and LWIR experiments support within-dataset applicability. These results support combined semantic regularization and spatial refinement, while paired repeated ablations, quantitative boundary assessment and cross-site validation remain necessary.

title: Frequency Decoupling and Recalibration for Small Object Detection in Remote Sensing Images via Discrete Wavelet Transform
abstract: The rapid advancement of deep learning has significantly improved the performance of remote sensing object detection. However, detection performance for small objects remains unsatisfactory. In this paper, we identify frequency aliasing as a key challenge underlying small object detection performance degradation and propose DWT-DETR, a novel frequency decoupling and recalibration small object detector using discrete wavelet transform (DWT). The proposed DWT-DETR employs DWT to obtain explicit frequency-band representations and further models them according to the different requirements of feature encoding and multi-scale feature fusion. In the feature encoding stage, we design a frequency-band mixing module (DWT-FBM) to mitigate the degradation of high-frequency details of small objects in deeper layers. The DWT-FBM first employs Haar wavelets to decompose features into frequency sub-bands, then applies cross-frequency interaction and dynamic amplitude modulation to adaptively recalibrate the frequency information. Finally, the refined features are reconstructed via inverse wavelet transform. During feature fusion, we design a frequency-guided fusion module (DWT-FGF) to ensure spatial alignment and discrimination of the fused features. The DWT-FGF employs a dual-path mechanism that decouples shallow features into low-frequency and high-frequency sub-bands via wavelet decomposition. The low-frequency sub-band serves as a spatial reference to guide deep upsampling and reduce geometric deformation, while the high-frequency sub-bands are used to suppress background noise. Extensive experiments on AI-TOD, DIOR, and VisDrone datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of DWT-DETR, which achieves 30.8% AP, 79.4% mAP, and 32.6% AP, respectively.

title: Predictive Line-of-Sight Geometry Compatibility in High-Rate GNSS: Formulation, Validity, and Causal Limits
abstract: High-rate Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) measurements can resolve dynamic motion, but detecting a spectral component does not identify its physical source. This study formulates Predictive Geometry-Normalized Structural Compatibility (PGNSC) as a post-detection, single-receiver test in which a model fitted without one satellite predicts the omitted complex time-differenced carrier-phase (TDCP) response through measured line-of-sight (LOS) geometry. PGNSC is characterised by the open TRANSFORM2 TM3 campaign, comprising 50 Hz GNSS observations and 47 controlled sinusoidal events at 0.5 and 2 Hz with independent accelerometers and additional GNSS receivers. Conventional variometric processing recovered the imposed frequencies; PGNSC then tested whether the detected response generalised through LOS geometry. Because the six-GPS formulation has limited redundancy and high leverage, a GPS+Galileo sensitivity analysis examined numerical robustness. It reduced PRESS fragility and yielded campaign-internal event-versus-quiet area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.959 at 0.5 Hz and 0.9998 at 2 Hz; separate dependence-aware checks on the historical expanded branch also retained strong separation. Algebraically, disturbances within the tested LOS-model space can preserve both fitted-model residuals and leave-one-satellite-out prediction errors. An exchangeable in-model-space verification accordingly produced chance-level discrimination (CPAUC = 0.491; 95% CI, 0.457–0.524). CP quantifies predictive LOS compatibility within the tested campaign; causal attribution requires independent physical evidence beyond LOS geometry.

title: Development of the Potential Evapotranspiration-Vegetation-Precipitation Drought Index (PETVPDI) and Its Application in West Africa Using Remote Sensing Datasets
abstract: Drought remains one of the most severe climate-related hazards affecting water resources, ecosystems, and agricultural productivity in West Africa (WA). Traditional drought indices often rely on individual hydroclimatic or vegetation variables and may not fully represent the coupled effects of precipitation supply, atmospheric evaporative demand, and vegetation response. To address this limitation, this study develops and applies a composite drought indicator, the Potential Evapotranspiration–Vegetation–Precipitation Drought Index (PETVPDI), using multi-source remote sensing datasets over WA for 2001–2022. PETVPDI integrates precipitation (P), potential evapotranspiration (PET), and the normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) within a three-dimensional Euclidean-distance framework. The index was evaluated against GLDAS soil moisture (SM), ESA CCI SM, gross primary productivity (GPP), and net primary productivity (NPP), and compared with four conventional remote-sensing drought indices (cRSDI): VCI, VHI, TVDI, and TVPDI. Deseasonalized anomaly correlations, used as the primary validation evidence to reduce the influence of the shared monsoon seasonal cycle, show that PETVPDI achieved the highest numerical correlations among the evaluated indices with GLDAS SM (R = 0.556, p < 0.001), ESA CCI SM (R = 0.513, p < 0.001), and GPP (R = 0.483, p < 0.001). Steiger’s tests for dependent overlapping correlations show that the PETVPDI–TVPDI difference was statistically significant for raw GLDAS SM and deseasonalized ESA CCI SM, but not for the other evaluated comparisons. Spatial PETVPDI patterns represent each pixel’s relative position within its own 2001–2022 hydroclimatic and vegetation range and therefore should not be interpreted as direct differences in absolute climatic aridity among locations. Long-term trends are spatially heterogeneous across WA. Overall, PETVPDI provides an integrated framework for monitoring relative drought–wetness variability and offers complementary information for drought assessment and early-warning applications in data-scarce regions.

title: Ori-INR: Orientation-Aware Implicit Neural Representation for Remote Sensing Image Representation
abstract: Implicit Neural Representations (INRs) model images as continuous functions that map spatial coordinates to pixel values, providing a compact and resolution-independent framework for image representation. Existing INR methods have achieved strong performance through coordinate-based modeling and activation design, enabling effective representation of complex visual signals. Remote sensing images provide a representative scenario where spatial orientation plays an important role in visual representation. Many structures, such as roads, rivers, and building boundaries, exhibit clear geometric layouts and orientation-dependent patterns, making orientation-aware modeling particularly important for accurate representation and interpretation. In this work, we propose Ori-INR, an orientation-aware implicit neural representation for remote sensing image representation. Ori-INR introduces explicit orientation modeling into coordinate-based networks from two complementary perspectives. First, we design an orientation-modulated activation that enables hidden representations to capture orientation-sensitive responses aligned with spatial structures. Second, we introduce a radial-angular coordinate encoding that integrates radial distance and angular phase information, providing explicit orientation-aware cues at the input level. By combining these two components, Ori-INR enhances the ability of INRs to represent orientation-structured visual signals in a more expressive and structured manner. Extensive experiments on multiple remote sensing benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed method consistently improves representation quality and better preserves geometric and directional structures compared with existing INR approaches.

title: Early-Season Avocado Yield Forecasting in New Zealand Using Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, and Climate Variables
abstract: Reliable pre-season yield forecasting remains a persistent challenge in avocado (Persea americana Mill.) production, due to strong year-to-year variation and alternate bearing. This study developed an early-season, block-level yield forecasting framework combining multi-temporal Sentinel-2 optical indices, Sentinel-1 SAR structural indices, TerraClimate variables and historical yield over a two-year lagged predictor window ending before the target season begins. The framework was applied to 252 commercial orchard blocks in the Bay of Plenty and Northland regions of New Zealand and evaluated on five production seasons (2020–2024). Five machine learning approaches, XGBoost, CatBoost, LightGBM, LSTM, and the tabular foundation model TabICL, were compared using Leave-One-Year-Out (LOYO) cross-validation. TabICL gave the strongest performance (RMSE = 2.80 ± 0.47 t ha−1, MAE = 2.12 ± 0.31 t ha−1, R2 = 0.85 ± 0.04). Extending the predictor window from one to two years, excluding historical yield information, reduced TabICL’s mean RMSE by approximately 1.32 t ha−1. SHAP analysis identified actual evapotranspiration and yield from two seasons earlier as the strongest predictors, with canopy structure and temperature also contributing. A pre-season yield map for 2024 shows the framework’s potential to support harvest scheduling, labour planning, and supply forecasting. Combining multi-source satellite time series with a biologically informed two-year yield lag offers a practical approach to early-season avocado yield forecasting, with potential for other perennial fruit crops.
