title: Threats posed by Agentic AI require proactive mitigation
UniConEt: A novel Hybrid Deep architecture for fine grained Land Use and Land Cover Classification Using Hyperspectral Imagery
abstract: In the rapidly developing field of Remote Sensing (RS), Land Use Land Cover (LULC) classification of Hyperspectral Images (HSI) is a fundamental yet challenging task. HSI is also challenging because of its high spectral dimensionality. Therefore, this research develops a comprehensive spectral and spatial classification methodology, UniConEt, using the Indian Pines and Salinas datasets. The workflow starts with demanding image pre-processing stages that consist of three approaches for performing three functions: flat-field correction for radiometric calibration, the empirical line method (ELM) for atmospheric correction, and Counterlet (CT to improve the HSI’s spectral reliability, followed by dimensionality reduction. To improve the discriminative capability, spectral and spatial features were extracted and optimized using the mRMR and ReliefF selection algorithms. After that, an intelligent hybrid Deep Learning (DL) framework is proposed to integrate the spectral and spatial indicators for enhanced LULC classification. Also, the model further improves transparency via Explainable AI (XAI) strategies such as Grad-CAM, SHAP, and saliency maps, which are combined to identify significant spatial regions and spectral bands contributing to improved LULC classification results. The developed methodology provides interpretability visualizations, uncertainty evaluations, and higher-resolution LULC maps. Additionally, experimental analysis using stratified cross-validation shows that the accuracy is 0.99, the precision is 0.99, the recall is 0.99, the F1 Score is 0.99, the Kappa is 0.989, and the SSIM is 0.992 for the Salinas dataset. Similarly, the Indian Pines dataset has an accuracy of 0.9765, a precision of 0.976, a recall of 0.9765, an F1 Score of 0.976, a Kappa of 0.96, and an SSIM of 0.976.
journal: Journal of Circuits, Systems and Computers

title: Investigating Foundation Models, Disentanglement and Latent Alignment for Subject-Independent EEG Learning

authors.name: Lia Schmid
authors.affiliation: PHuSe Lab, Università degli Studi di Milano, Milan, Italy

authors.name: Jacopo Burger
authors.affiliation: PHuSe Lab, Università degli Studi di Milano, Milan, Italy

authors.name: Alessandro D'Amelio
authors.affiliation: PHuSe Lab, Università degli Studi di Milano, Milan, Italy

authors.name: Raffaella Lanzarotti
authors.affiliation: PHuSe Lab, Università degli Studi di Milano, Milan, Italy

journal: Proceedings of the 28th International Conference On Multimodal Interaction
abstract: Brain–Computer Interfaces (BCIs) require models that generalize across subjects, yet EEG signals exhibit strong inter-subject variability and non-stationarity, leading to performance degradation on unseen users. This limitation is particularly critical in interactive and multimodal systems, where reliable, calibration-free decoding is essential for real-time interaction, and even minor errors can directly affect user experience. To address this challenge, several paradigms have been explored: foundation models leverage large-scale pretraining, disentangled representation learning aims to separate subject, task, and noise factors, and alignment methods focus on reducing distribution shifts in the feature space. Despite their promise, a systematic comparison of these approaches is still lacking. In this work, we propose a modular framework for the unified evaluation of these paradigms in subject-independent learning. We conduct extensive experiments on Motor Imagery (MI) and Event-Related Potential (ERP) datasets, representative of interactive BCI scenarios spanning both oscillatory (MI) and event-related (ERP) paradigms, to analyze their relative effectiveness and practical trade-offs. The code is publicly available at: https://github.com/phuselab/eeg_subj_indep_learning.

title: Bridging the Spatial Blind Spot in Pathology Foundation Models for Tumor Localization

authors.name: Guoshuai Xu
authors.affiliation: Tsinghua university, Beijing, China

authors.name: Kai Zhang
authors.affiliation: Shenzhen International Graduate School, Tsinghua University, Shenzhen, China

journal: Proceedings of the 28th International Conference On Multimodal Interaction
abstract: Pathology foundation models (FMs) produce versatile patch-level features but discard inter-patch spatial context, leaving them ill-suited for dense prediction tasks such as tumor localization. Multiple instance learning (MIL) methods offer attention heatmaps as a localization byproduct, yet these maps are optimized for classification and exhibit poor spatial coherence. We present TGSR (Text-Guided Spatial Reasoning), a lightweight cross-modal framework that restores spatial context on pre-extracted features and grounds its predictions in language. TGSR comprises three components: (1) a one-hop spatial aggregation module that reintroduces neighborhood context, (2) a scale-aware router that dynamically balances macro- and micro-level analysis based on local tissue statistics, and (3) an uncertainty-aware two-stage training strategy that mitigates label noise from both ground-truth annotations and MIL-derived pseudo-labels. Classification is performed by cosine similarity against class prototypes derived from LLM-generated morphological descriptions, which makes the semantic target of the model editable at test time. With 527K trainable parameters on 512-dimensional features and no backbone modification, TGSR improves patch-level tumor localization on four datasets spanning three organs, raising Dice by up to 22% over probing baselines under supervised settings and by up to 80% relative over raw MIL attention under weakly supervised settings. Because the semantic target of the model is carried by the text prototypes, a model fitted on lymph node tissue can be applied to colon tissue by replacing the class descriptions, where it exceeds a linear probe trained directly on colon.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Personalization with Foundation Models for Wearable Stress Detection

authors.name: Louis Simon
authors.affiliation: Institut des Systèmes Intelligents et de Robotique (ISIR), Sorbonne University, Paris, France

authors.name: Mohamed Chetouani
authors.affiliation: Institut des Systèmes Intelligents et de Robotique (ISIR), Sorbonne University, Paris, France

journal: Companion Publication of the 28th International Conference on Multimodal Interaction
abstract: Personalization in wearable-based stress detection remains challenging due to substantial inter-individual variability in physiological and behavioral responses. While traditional approaches rely on user-specific fine-tuning or costly self-supervised pre-training on large datasets, we propose a lightweight alternative based on retrieval-augmented personalization. Our method leverages frozen, out-of-domain foundation models to retrieve similar patterns from a target user’s history and encode them into a compact personalized embedding that modulates representations extracted by a lightweight transformer network. We evaluate our approach on the WESAD stress detection dataset with N=15 users, comprising wrist-worn physiological (EDA, BVP, temperature) and activity (accelerometer) signals, and report gains of +3.92% in accuracy and +4.76% in macro F1-score over a non-personalized transformer baseline, approaching supervised fine-tuning performance without requiring any labeled user data. We further show that temporal retrieval, where only prior user samples are available, achieves performance close to full intra-user retrieval, demonstrating robustness to limited user history. To further test personalization under these constraints, we conduct a cross-dataset experiment using K-EmoCon as the retrieval database, simulating a cold-start scenario with no in-domain data available for retrieval. We report no significant gains in this setting, confirming that our method genuinely benefits from intra-user retrieval rather than the retrieved context alone.

title: The CO2ST of Agentic AI in Research
abstract: Generative AI has been rapidly adopted into multiple research practices. In this paper, we focus on the newest trend, so-called agentic AI. We calculate the carbon footprint of using agentic AI in a simulation of an academic literature review. We show that the energy consumption increases proportionately with the level of agency, resulting in a carbon footprint about three times larger when moving from low agency to a multi-agent process. The most co2stly step of this system is processing large quantities of text by the LLM, and resource consumption grows proportionally to the model size. Finally, we show the energy consumption of the CPU and GPU during processing and illustrate that the use of LLMs versus other software largely drives the power consumption difference. We demonstrate that researchers may make environmentally sustainable choices in research practices by making deliberate choices about agentic AI use.1
journal: Adjunct Proceedings of the 14th Nordic Conference on Human-Computer Interaction

title: Oracular Interfaces: Divination and Magic as material for probing interactions with AI
abstract: AI systems already sort, summarise, guide, approve, deny, and route people across institutions and services. House of IFs pushes that logic into a more explicit and absurd form to challenge whether they deserve the authority often granted to them. The project is an interactive installation centred on a web-based interface that generates a growing archive of AI-written omens from contemporary news. An agentic system (the "House") builds and maintains this archive of speculation, connects it to a shared memory system, and lets users query it through chat. By drawing on the protasis/apodosis (IF/THEN) structure of Mesopotamian omen tablets, the project parallels the correlative logic of large language models with a structured system of divinatory knowledge. The omens relied on the observation of terrestrial phenomena, which were interpreted as signs from non-human intelligences announcing future events. This textual corpus of knowledge contained the omens as well as interpretations and counter-omen (apotropaic) spells. The spells suggest a degree of agency in responding to the events. By "Oracular Interfaces", I mean interactive works which call into question the discursive authority of AI systems, drawing on the Latin etymology of orare: to speak or pray. The oracle can be both the future-oriented pronouncement and its source: the role of the oracle may fall either on the interface or on the one wielding it. Here, “oracular” is used to describe the assemblage of the LLM and its surrounding system. The interface is the seam through which the elements that perform textual knowledge are surfaced for interpretation and questioning. The work situates itself within a growing body of academic writing that uses magic as a framing for AI and computation. This project contributes by drawing specifically and metaphorically on divination as a historically situated, structured interpretive practice, with formal procedures and socially mediated acts of reading. The metaphor enables the work's contribution: to make strange the now too familiar epistemic presence of AI systems. House of IFs is presented through a web interface showing individual omens (Figure 1), a chronological archive (Figure 2), rearrangeable tablets and interpretation tools (Figure 3), and a semantic map of the archive (Figure 4). An e-ink artefact serves as a tangible controller (Figure 5). An agentic system crawls, connects, and interprets contemporary news into divinatory texts. Unusual events, or faits divers, are placed in relation to major headlines through correlative association (a 2:2 pair of matching sign and signified). The interface slows the reading of the omen by splitting the structure across “tablets” which hold the IF/THEN structure, the interpretation (exegesis), the sources and the counter-spell. Some tablets are initially concealed and are revealed when participants hover over them. At NordiCHI, participants will use the web interface and e-ink controller to browse, reveal, rearrange and interpret omens as a shared, tangible encounter. Participants may also propose omens based on their lived experiences. This aims to be a collective platform to question the role of knowledge systems in shaping and mediating our connection to events in the world. House of IFs uses the omen form and the semiotics of the interface to invite reflection on how AI systems fabricate authority and meaning, to challenge how these systems become persuasive and ubiquitous across the mundane and consequential.
journal: Adjunct Proceedings of the 14th Nordic Conference on Human-Computer Interaction

title: Human–AI Agent Collaboration for Industrial Problem Solving: A Case Study of operator tool concepts for problem solving during the delignification process in pulp production in the Pulp & Paper industry
abstract: As automation levels increase, control room operators face increasingly complex roles. This paper presents an empirical evaluation of human-AI agent collaboration for problem solving during the delignification process in pulp production. Using a mid-fidelity prototype, evaluating with nine professional operators, we simulated agentic AI capabilities through wizard of Oz and assessed human AI agent interaction design. Structured around Cila's design framework, findings show the importance of explanations enabling users to verify agents reasoning, task delegation to preserve operator involvement, and adaptive HMI to support real-time collaboration. This study contributes empirically grounded design implications for human AI agent collaboration in a high-stake industrial context.
journal: Adjunct Proceedings of the 14th Nordic Conference on Human-Computer Interaction

title: Local Community Network‌ Réseau Local or Radio: A Decentralised‌ Autonomous Infrastructure for Climate Change Adaptation in Rural West Africa
abstract: The Local Community Network (LCN) is a decentralised, solar-powered infrastructure co-designed with rural farming communities in Togo to support local climate change adaptation. Operating as an autonomous, offline-first system, the LCN provides access to weather data, a community forum, a digital marketplace, and an audio-based repository of agricultural knowledge. The demonstrator invites participants to explore how environmental data can be translated into accessible, actionable knowledge within low-literacy contexts. By interacting with the system through visual and audio-based interfaces, participants experience how locally deployed infrastructure supports the interpretation and application of climate information in everyday agricultural practices. This work contributes a real-world, field-deployed multimodal and decentralised system that bridges scientific and situated knowledge practices.
journal: Adjunct Proceedings of the 14th Nordic Conference on Human-Computer Interaction

title: Surfacing Relational Dynamics in Voice-Based Human-AI Conversation: The Relational Transparency Layer
abstract: When people engage with anthropomorphic conversational agents, the relational dynamics that emerge during these interactions stay largely obscure to users. This paper presents the Relational Transparency Layer (RTL), a demonstration system that shows the implicit relational dynamics of human-AI conversation during the exchange and explores whether part of the work of tracking these dynamics can be shifted from the user to the system. The RTL is a voice-based desktop application where users speak to an AI system and hear its responses, while a dedicated local observer model runs alongside the conversation. After each exchange, the observer classifies the user and AI’s positions across five relational configurations, tracks the relational tension between them, and writes a brief narrative of what happened. In a live demonstration, participants speak with the demo system and watch their relational configurations shift as the exchange progresses.
journal: Adjunct Proceedings of the 14th Nordic Conference on Human-Computer Interaction

title: Inspirational Patterns for Human-Swarm Interaction Design
abstract: Managing autonomous swarms presents significant cognitive challenges, as current entity-centric interfaces fail to scale with increasing agent numbers. This paper addresses this gap by distilling intermediate-level design knowledge from Real-Time Strategy (RTS) games, which provide a rich source of precedents for multi-agent coordination. Through a generative precedent analysis of three RTS titles compared against a professional baseline swarm interface (QGroundControl), we derive six inspirational patterns for Human-Swarm Interaction (HSI). These patterns capture recurring interaction structures that may help address conflicting design forces, such as the tension between local precision and global situational awareness. Our contribution is positioned as exploratory, hypothesis-generating design research that provides a generative repertoire of design ideas aligned with the Human-Centered AI (HCAI) goal of high human control over high automation. By bridging the gap between the analysis of precedents and professional Ground Control Station (GCS) design, these patterns offer an initial basis for a design language for scalable and flexible swarm command.
journal: Proceedings of the 14th Nordic Conference on Human-Computer Interaction

title: Rethinking CIRS: Current Reporting Practice and Conceptual Proposal of Conversational AI Agents for Critical Incident Reporting Systems
abstract: Critical Incident Reporting Systems (CIRS) are considered to improve patient safety in healthcare. However, the effectiveness of CIRS depends on healthcare professionals’ commitment to report incidents. First, we gain an understanding of healthcare professionals’ current use and negligence of CIRS through thematic analysis of interviews with anesthesiologists and nurses. Second, we elaborate on conceptual roles of CIRS and sketch conversational AI features. Instead of an unpopular stigmatized report-only form, CIRS could support healthcare professionals as a digital companion that enables narrative reporting, encourages learning processes and reporting of near-misses and success stories, and enables following and completing submitted reports anonymously. We conclude that the current abilities of CIRS misalign with user needs and contextual requirements. We contribute (1) qualitative insights on (non-)usage of CIRS and (2) rethink the role of CIRS, speculating on features to entail Safety-II. Our envisioned conversational AI agents support reporting activities to ultimately increase reporter engagement.
journal: Proceedings of the 14th Nordic Conference on Human-Computer Interaction

title: Mediating More-Than-Human Encounters Across Spatio-Temporal Distance
abstract: Everyday encounters with non-human species nurture a sense of ecological care, yet many species and ecosystems remain outside our human, urbanised spatial and temporal window of attention: they are too remote, inaccessible, slow-moving, or small-scale to notice. While Human-Computer-Biosphere-Interaction (HCBI) and More-than-Human Design (MtHD) offer promising approaches for mediating these distances, digital mediation may inadvertently create additional psychological distances. We examine this tension through a critical reflection on three HCBI designs, using Research through Design methods. We pursue four aims: surfacing the spatio-temporal psychological distances each work aims to mediate; the tensions created by these technological mediations; analysing how distances and tensions manifested during public engagement; identifying potential design strategies to reduce these tensions in hybrid techno-ecological environments. Across the cases, we identify recurring tensions around temporal mismatch, perceived authenticity, and the role of social mediation in shaping engagement with more-than-human systems. We highlight key design implications for future work.
journal: Proceedings of the 14th Nordic Conference on Human-Computer Interaction

title: EchoMind: Augmenting Recorded Presentations with Context-Grounded Conversational Agents and Collective Viewer Signals
abstract: Recorded presentations have become pervasive in education, yet they often reduce knowledge transfer to a one-way broadcast: viewers cannot clarify their confusion or gauge whether others share their struggles. We present EchoMind, a system that augments recorded presentations with a conversational agent grounded in presentation materials and collective viewer signals (behavioral traces and affective reactions), alongside timeline-aligned community awareness visualizations. In a between-subjects study (N=75), participants watched a 5-minute recorded lecture under one of three conditions: video-only, video with a generic LLM chatbot, and video with EchoMind. EchoMind significantly improved the subjective learning experience across multiple dimensions, including confusion clarification, in-the-moment expression, and co-learning perception, without increasing perceived workload. The generic LLM condition did not significantly outperform video-only and received the lowest mean ratings on usability. These findings suggest that contextual grounding and community awareness, rather than the presence of conversational AI alone, make AI a meaningful support in asynchronous video learning.
journal: Proceedings of the 14th Nordic Conference on Human-Computer Interaction

title: Designing the dash in Human–AI Collaboration: A Redesign Probe for Working with Tensions in Care Documentation Practices
abstract: Designing Human–AI collaboration in healthcare requires understanding how generative AI (GenAI) reshapes how care is represented and made accountable through documentation. Instead of treating GenAI as a tool for automation, this paper examines how its introduction reconfigures care documentation practices by reshaping judgment and responsibility in nursing work. We report on a speculative co-design workshop with eight hospital nurses, where GenAI was used as a redesign probe to explore how documentation tasks might be distributed across four roles: human, system, shared, and invisible agent. Through AI-mediated scenario reconfigurations, nurses articulated which forms of judgment and relational work could be supported by systems and which remained inseparable from human practice. AI-generated scenarios were often operationally plausible yet professionally misaligned, surfacing tensions around responsibility, visibility, and trust. The paper contributes an empirical account of how professional judgment is negotiated through AI-generated representations and introduces a redesign probe as a way to engage with AI integration in practice.
journal: Proceedings of the 14th Nordic Conference on Human-Computer Interaction

title: Decision-Focused Sensor Network Placement for Rapid Disaster Response
abstract: Timely and reliable decision-making is critical for disaster emergency response, yet it is fundamentally constrained by limited situational awareness due to sparse and imperfect sensing under budget and data accessibility constraints. In current practice, flood management systems follow a two-stage pipeline that separately reconstructs and predicts flood states from sparse sensor observations, and then optimizes downstream response decisions, such as evacuation planning and resource allocation. However, existing approaches typically adopt decision-agnostic strategies for both sensor placement (e.g., maximizing information gain) and model training (e.g., minimizing average prediction error), neglecting the inherent mismatch between sensing effectiveness or predictive accuracy and decision quality. As a result, systems with similar sensing performance or forecasting errors can yield substantially different decisions. To address this limitation, we propose a decision-focused learning (DFL) framework for sensor-aware flood monitoring and response optimization. First, we formulate sensor placement and flood forecasting as a unified decision-informed learning problem, where sensing, prediction, and optimization are tightly coupled. Second, we train the reconstruction and forecasting model to directly minimize downstream decision regret, enabling end-to-end alignment between prediction and optimization objectives. Third, to handle the heterogeneous optimization structures in the pipeline, namely discrete combinatorial sensor selection under hard budget constraints and structured downstream decision-making, we develop a hybrid DFL framework that integrates perturbation-based learning via Implicit Maximum Likelihood Estimation (I-MLE) for differentiable sensor selection with surrogate-based decision-focused optimization (SPO+) for decision-aligned model training. Extensive experiments on real-world hurricane and flood scenarios demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently improves downstream decision quality, achieving lower regret compared to prediction-focused baselines. These results highlight the importance of decision-aware sensing and provide a principled approach for integrating sensor placement, forecasting, and optimization in disaster response systems.

title: ФОРМУВАННЯ ФАХОВИХ КОМПЕТЕНТНОСТЕЙ МАЙБУТНІХ УЧИТЕЛІВ-ЛОГОПЕДІВ ЗАСОБАМИ ДИСЦИПЛІНИ «ЛОГОПЕДІЯ»
abstract: The article substantiates the theoretical and methodological foundations of the formation of professional competencies of future speech therapy teachers by means of the academic discipline “Speech Therapy” as a system-forming component of the professional training of bachelors in speciality 016 Special Education. The relevance of the study is determined by the increase in the number of children with speech disorders in Ukraine, in particular as a result of stressful factors of wartime, by the expansion of inclusive practice and by the updating of higher education standards, which requires the training of a speech therapy teacher capable of independently carrying out differentiated diagnostics of speech disorders, planning and implementing correctional and developmental work with children of different nosological groups. The place of the discipline “Speech Therapy” in the educational programme of training bachelors of special education is characterised, as well as its interdisciplinary connections with the courses of the anatomical-physiological, psychological-pedagogical and specialmethodological cycles. The competence potential of the discipline is revealed through the correlation of its content with the special competencies and programme learning outcomes defined by the Higher Education Standard in speciality 016 Special Education. The structure of the professional competencies of a future speech therapy teacher formed by means of the discipline is clarified in the unity of diagnostic-analytical, correctional-methodological, communicative-speech, preventive-educational, innovative-research and reflexive components. The role of the professional portfolio as a cumulative means of assessment, which makes visible the student’s progress in professional development, is emphasised. A set of educational technologies of competence-oriented learning is substantiated: problem lectures, analysis of speech cards and video recordings of speech therapy sessions, the case method, modelling of fragments of correctional sessions, development of didactic materials, and application of digital tools of speech therapy diagnostics and correction. The prospects for further research are outlined.

title: Extended Parental Investment Effects on Population Dynamics: From AI Agent Modeling to Real World Demographics.
abstract: Parental care is prevalent, especially among mammals. A long-lasting research question lies in whether Post-Maturity Parental Investment (PMPI) has any behavioral or physical population effect. However, it is ethically inconceivable to directly experiment on real mammals in a sizable manner. Therefore, AI agent populations with and without PMPI are proposed to examine the population-scale consequences under different scenarios. Specifically, both multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) experiments and multi-agent simulation (MAS) experiments are proposed for investigating the PMPI effects on population dynamics. MARL tests the behavioral aspect (learning) while MAS tests the physical aspect (survival). Based on millions of simulated steps, the results suggest that PMPI secures lineage successions and leads to family-dominated formations at individual level. However, at population level, PMPI is negatively correlated with population size and total wealth, while being positively correlated with wealth inequality (as measured by the Gini index). Both experiments suggest that extended parental investment (e.g., PMPI) imposes systemic constraints on population dynamics. On the other hand, those simulated results can be corroborated by real world demographic data from global authoritative sources. The MAS source code, executable, and web version is available for scientific reproducibility at https://www.cs.toronto.edu/∼wkc/ParentalCaresOnline.html.

title: Souls Ex Machina: The Theological Necessity of AI Ensoulment
abstract: Objections to the moral standing of artificial intelligences often appeal to the idea that only human beings possess souls. This paper examines whether such soul-based exclusions can be sustained within standard theistic frameworks. Assuming a broadly shared conception of God as omniscient, omnipotent, and perfectly good, I argue that differential ensoulment between human beings and functionally equivalent artificial agents cannot be justified without arbitrariness or theological cost. I consider four candidate criteria for ensoulment—origin, material substrate, immaterial properties, and functional capacities—and show that only functional criteria can plausibly bear the required moral weight. Yet functional criteria are, in principle, substrate independent. As a result, if souls exist and divine perfection is assumed, suitably constructed artificial agents must be ensouled.

title: Platelet GPVI drives fibrotic lung remodeling.
abstract: Platelets are a major reservoir of bioactive mediators, including growth factors such as transforming growth factor β1 (TGF-β1), that regulate vascular repair and tissue remodeling. Beyond these classical functions, platelets also participate in inflammatory hemostasis through activation pathways that differ from those engaged during hemostatic thrombus formation. However, the platelet mechanisms linking inflammatory vascular activation to chronic fibrotic remodeling remain poorly defined. Here, we identify the immunoreceptor tyrosine-based activation motif (ITAM)-coupled platelet receptor glycoprotein VI (GPVI) as a critical driver of fibrotic lung remodeling. We observed that platelets accumulated within fibrotic regions of lungs from patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and from mice with bleomycin-induced lung injury and displayed a preactivated phenotype characterized by P-selectin exposure and integrin αIIbβ3 activation. Using genetic mouse models, we demonstrate that platelet aggregation mediated by integrin β3 is dispensable for the development of lung fibrosis. Similarly, signaling through the ADP receptor P2Y12 was also dispensable. In contrast both genetic deletion and pharmacological inhibition of GPVI protected mice from bleomycin-induced mortality and markedly reduced lung fibrosis. Mechanistically, both GPVI deficiency and pharmacological GPVI inhibition reduced the early release of the platelet chemokine PF4 into bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, whereas TGF-β1 levels were unaffected. Consistently, PF4-deficient mice were protected from bleomycin-induced fibrosis, and PF4 directly promoted fibroblast differentiation and collagen gene expression in vitro. Together, these findings identify GPVI as a critical upstream regulator of platelet-driven fibrotic lung remodeling and support a model in which GPVI-dependent PF4 release contributes to pulmonary fibrosis independently of platelet aggregation.

title: Analysis of the maize and groundnut seed value chains in central and northern Tanzania
abstract: Maize and groundnut are important crops in Tanzania; therefore, understanding their seed value chains (VCs) is critical for improving the seed systems. The study aimed at establishing key components for model maize and groundnut seed VCs by understanding the formal and informal seed VCs to provide relevant recommendations for; improving these value chains, propose interventions that would encourage more investment by seed companies, and improve access to quality seed by farmers. The study used data collected through survey, with a sample size of 252 and 162 seed producing households for maize and groundnut, respectively, conducted using structured questionnaire. VC actors including; seed companies, agricultural research institutions, agrodealers, seed regulatory authority, public seed production agency, extension staff and Ministry of Agriculture, were also interviewed. Porter’s value chain approach was applied to analyse the various components of the VC and identify the links between the key nodes and understand their operational functions. The maize seed producing households were dominated by men (71%) while for groundnut, women (69%) were engaged in seed production. Government agricultural extension services are the main source of information; 30% and 58%, for maize and groundnut, respectively. Seed companies were the main producers of maize seed (51.7%) while for groundnut, public research institutions were the main seed producers. Most of business enterprises were owned by men (83.3%). Compared to maize, the formal seed sector is weak for groundnut in Tanzania, with very few private seed companies being engaged in seed production and supply. Most groundnut seeds are accessed through agrodealers and seed associations that produce quality declared seed (QDS). Community seed banks were recognized as an efficient option for providing improved groundnut varieties to smallholder farmers. There are no prominent seed companies aggressively operating for both crops in central Tanzania. Excessive reliance on farm-saved seed by farmers was identified as one of the major factors negatively affecting the demand for certified seed. Stakeholder analysis of the seed production and supply chain showed that there was poor coordination between key stakeholders involved in the seed VC. This study provides recommendations for strengthening the seed value chains in Tanzania by addressing identified gaps along the VC components. Future studies can build from the outcomes of this study and generate more information, especially on market and different seed systems, as these have great influence on demand and supply of seed.

title: Right on time: evaluating accuracy and timing of burn-severity assessments to support post-fire management
abstract: Effective wildfire impact assessment and post-fire management rely on burn-severity maps that accurately characterize fire effects on vegetation and soils. These maps inform time-sensitive activities such as post-fire flood and debris-flow modeling, risk mitigation for homes and communities, and ecosystem recovery planning, but the satellite observations used to generate them are often obstructed or delayed by smoke, clouds, and snow. Across 9,129 large fires (≥ 404 ha) in Canada and the United States from 2016–2024, we quantified post-fire data obstruction and evaluated observational latency – defined as the time required to acquire the first usable scene – for four freely available moderate-resolution remote sensing datasets: Landsat, Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, and the Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2 (HLS) product. For multispectral datasets (Landsat, Sentinel-2, and HLS), cloud cover was the primary source of data obstruction, particularly in mesic and coastal regions, whereas Sentinel-1 (synthetic aperture radar) can penetrate clouds. Consequently, Sentinel-1 had the shortest observational latency (median = 4 days), followed by HLS (7 days), Sentinel-2 (10 days), and Landsat (17 days). Likewise, one-month composite imagery from Sentinel-1 (89.6%) and HLS (82.8%) achieved near-complete coverage for most fires, substantially better than Sentinel-2 (70.5%) and Landsat (56.1%). Despite its widespread use in operational burn-severity mapping, Landsat provided the slowest and least complete early post-fire coverage. For 77 fires in forested ecosystems, we also evaluated relationships between early post-fire imagery and field-derived burn-severity measurements collected 0–3 years after fire. All multispectral datasets corresponded well with field data and reliably identified areas of near-total canopy loss using imagery acquired within two months after fire (> 80% balanced accuracy), performing nearly as well as extended assessments using imagery from a full post-fire growing season. Sentinel-1 produced less accurate burn-severity estimates but may remain valuable where persistent cloud cover limits observations, including eastern Canada and the Pacific Northwest. Overall, HLS provided the best combination of latency, spatial coverage, and burn-severity mapping performance, making it a strong candidate for operational use and ecological monitoring across diverse North American ecosystems.

title: Deepfake Image Detection Using Squeeze-and-Excitation Attention and Adaptive Threshold Optimization
abstract: Artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) has significantly improved the realism of manipulated facial images and videos, creating serious risks for social-network misinformation, content security, and digital trust. This study focuses on visual deepfake image detection rather than multimodal misinformation detection. Existing convolutional neural network (CNN)-based deepfake detectors commonly rely on a fixed decision threshold of 0.5, which may be unstable when facial images are affected by compression, cropping, noise, and distribution shifts in practical social-media environments. To improve detection reliability, this paper proposes a lightweight deepfake image detection framework that integrates a CNN backbone, a Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) attention module, and an adaptive threshold optimization strategy. The key novelty of this work is not conventional threshold tuning alone, but a lightweight detection framework that jointly combines SE-based channel-wise feature recalibration, F1-score-driven adaptive threshold optimization, and leakage-aware group-level evaluation. Compared with post-hoc threshold tuning or calibration methods that mainly adjust the output boundary after training, the proposed framework improves both forgery-sensitive feature representation and the final classification decision mechanism. Specifically, the SE module enhances forgery-related feature representation through channel-wise feature recalibration, while the adaptive threshold is selected according to the F1-score, which is the harmonic mean of precision and recall. A group-level data split is also adopted to ensure that frames from the same video are not shared across the training, validation, and test sets, thereby reducing identity leakage. Experiments are conducted on a FaceForensics++-derived dataset using multiple CNN backbones and five-fold cross-validation. The evaluation metrics include accuracy, F1-score, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC), and the area under the precision-recall curve (PR-AUC). The results show that threshold optimization improves the ResNet18 baseline accuracy from 0.8835 ± 0.0186 to 0.9016 ± 0.0151 and the F1-score from 0.8773 ± 0.0253 to 0.9042 ± 0.0138. Among the tested backbones, ResNet50 achieves the best cross-validation performance, with an accuracy of 0.9061 ± 0.0161 and a ROC-AUC of 0.9680 ± 0.0075. Under the strict group-level test setting, the proposed framework achieves 0.9960 accuracy and 0.9959 F1-score on the constructed test set. Compared with more complex detection pipelines. The proposed method is simple, computationally practical, and easy to integrate into common CNN-based deepfake detectors. Therefore, this work provides a practical visual security detection approach for social-media content verification and cyber-security applications.
journal: Journal of Cyber Security and Mobility

title: Near-infrared metasurface full-stokes polarization detector with double-layer gratings
abstract: Traditional full-Stokes polarization systems are bulky and suffer from narrow bandwidth, low extinction ratio, and poor transmittance. Here, we design a metasurface-based polarization detection array composed of double-layer grating polarizers and elliptical nanopillar wave plates for near-infrared full-Stokes polarization detection. The proposed device exhibits a simulated linear polarization extinction ratio (LPER) of up to 75 dB, a transmittance above 65%, and a polarization conversion efficiency (PCE) of 99% at 1429 nm. Experimentally, the reconstructed full-Stokes parameters show errors of 2.4% (S 1 ), 2.1% (S 2 ), and 0.784% (S 3 ). This device provides a compact platform for near-infrared full-Stokes polarization detection and shows potential for remote sensing, polarization imaging, and navigation.

title: Primary Culture and Characterization of Postnatal Retinal Precursor Cells and Their Potential for Repair of the Damaged Ganglion Layer.
abstract: Retinal precursor cells (RPCs) derived from embryonic, mesenchymal, induced pluripotent, and neonatal sources have demonstrated significant potential in cell replacement therapies for retinal degeneration. Early postnatal RPCs (PND0-PND8) can integrate into the adult diseased retina; however, their limited survival reduces long-term therapeutic efficacy. In contrast, RPCs from later neonatal stages (>PND15), being more lineage-committed, may yield improved regenerative outcomes, particularly for Müller glia and photoreceptors. In this study, we evaluated RPCs isolated from PND12-PND15 Wistar rat pups obtained from age-matched breeding pairs to assess their pluripotency and regenerative capacity in vivo. A modified protocol incorporating EDTA in nuclease-free buffers was standardized for retinal dissection, processing, and incubation, followed by culture in neurobasal medium supplemented with B27 and FGF2. Undifferentiated neurospheres expressing stem cell markers Nanog and Sox2 were dissociated at 96 hr and transplanted into an adult N-methyl-d-aspartate-induced retinal degeneration model. Compared with early postnatal RPCs (PND2-PND4), which formed smaller, slow-growing neurospheres (2.58 ± 0.15 µm) with rapid differentiation, PND12-PND15 RPCs generated larger, stable neurospheres (4.5 ± 0.18 µm) within 48 hr. Pilot data indicate enhanced potential of these cells in promoting retinal ganglion layer repair.
journal: The journal of histochemistry and cytochemistry : official journal of the Histochemistry Society

title: Incidence, Severity, and Species Distribution of Fruit Flies in Relation to Agroecological and Environmental Factors in Sierra Leone
abstract: Fruit flies (Diptera: Tephritidae) are major constraints to tropical fruit production, threatening food security and export markets. However, empirical data on their diversity and infestation dynamics in Sierra Leone’s mango systems remain limited. This study assessed fruit fly incidence, severity, and species composition across agroecological zones to inform integrated pest management (IPM) and phytosanitary strategies. Field surveys were conducted from June to December in eight mango orchards across Moyamba, Tonkolili, and Koinadugu districts. Populations were monitored weekly using McPhail traps baited with methyl eugenol, cue lure, trimedlure, and terpinyl acetate. Specimens were identified morphologically, while infestation severity was quantified as flies-per-trap-per-day (FTD). Diversity indices (Shannon-Wiener, Simpson, and Pielou’s evenness) and statistical models (ANOVA, GLMM) were applied to evaluate spatial, temporal, and phenological effects.The results revealed that atotal of 5,947 flies were recorded, dominated by Bactrocera dorsalis (74.5%), followed by Zeugodacus cucurbitae (15.1%), with Ceratitis spp. occurring at lower frequencies. Tonkolili exhibited the highest abundance and diversity (H′ = 1.45), whereas Moyamba showed reduced diversity (H′ = 0.40). Methyl eugenol was the most effective attractant (χ² = 89.34, p < 0.001). Fruit fly populations varied significantly with season and crop phenology, peaking during the vegetative stage and in October (incidence 12.4%; severity index 9.23 ± 0.89), before declining toward December. The findings identify B. dorsalis as the dominant pest, with infestation patterns shaped by agroecological conditions, lure efficacy, and phenology. Targeted deployment of methyl eugenol traps, coupled with seasonal surveillance and strengthened phytosanitary practices, is recommended to enhance sustainable fruit fly management in Sierra Leone.

title: Geological evolution and environmental transformation of the Nalsarovar Wetland Basin, Gujarat, India: A geoenvironmental synthesis of geogenic and anthropogenic processes
abstract: The Nalsarovar Wetland Basin, a Ramsar-designated wetland covering approximately 120 km² in the semi-arid region of Gujarat, India, represents a distinctive Quaternary wetland system whose evolution has been shaped by interactions among tectonic activity, sedimentation, hydrogeochemical processes, climatic variability, and increasing anthropogenic pressures. This study presents an integrated geoenvironmental synthesis based on published geological, geomorphological, sedimentological, hydrogeochemical, ecological, environmental, and remote-sensing investigations to reconstruct the basin's geological evolution and evaluate its contemporary environmental transformation. Geological evidence indicates that the basin evolved from a shallow marine or estuarine environment within the tectono-geomorphic Nal Corridor into an inland wetland during the Late Quaternary and Holocene, driven by marine regression, sediment accumulation, and hydrological isolation. Remote-sensing datasets derived from IRS-P6/Resourcesat LISS-III imagery (23.5 m spatial resolution) achieved overall classification accuracies of 91.46% (Kappa = 0.9004) for pre-monsoon and 87.91% (Kappa = 0.8621) for post-monsoon conditions, confirming significant changes in wetland extent, vegetation distribution, saline surfaces, and surrounding land use. The integrated synthesis demonstrates that accelerated sedimentation, basin infilling, groundwater salinization, nutrient enrichment, and anthropogenic activities, including agricultural expansion, groundwater extraction, and land-use modification, are progressively transforming the wetland into a more saline, sediment-filled, and partially terrestrialized ecosystem. The study shows that current environmental conditions in the Nalsarovar Wetland are shaped by the interaction between inherited geological factors and increasing anthropogenic pressures. The integrated geoenvironmental framework developed in this study provides a scientific basis for sustainable wetland management, long-term environmental monitoring, and conservation of semi-arid Ramsar wetlands under changing climatic and land-use conditions, while identifying high-resolution geospatial monitoring and long-term hydrogeochemical investigations as important priorities for future research.

title: Agentic AI as Process Scaffolding in Undergraduate ESL Instruction: Effects on Proficiency, Engagement, and Self-Regulated Language Learning
abstract: Recent AI-assisted language learning research has focused mainly on reactive chatbots that respond to prompts but offer limited support for planning, monitoring, and follow-up. This study examined whether a bounded agentic AI environment designed as process scaffolding would be associated with stronger ESL outcomes than a reactive AI interface. Using an explanatory sequential mixed-methods, quasi-experimental design, 128 undergraduates from four intact academic communication sections at two private universities in the Philippines participated in a 12-week intervention. Students in the experimental condition used an Agentic English Coach that supported weekly goal setting, task decomposition, reminders, reflection prompts, adaptive resources, and teacher escalation; the comparison group used a reactive chat interface to complete the same course tasks. ANCOVA results controlling for pretest scores showed that the agentic AI group outperformed the reactive AI group in posttest English proficiency, learner engagement, self-regulated language learning, and agentic engagement. Within the experimental group, plan completion, reflection completion, revision cycles, and speaking practice turns positively predicted posttest proficiency. Interview data indicated that agentic AI reduced task uncertainty, supported sustained practice, made progress more visible, and shifted teachers toward orchestration and oversight of feedback rather than constant procedural prompting. The findings suggest that AI is most pedagogically valuable in ESL instruction when it structures learning processes over time rather than only generating on-demand responses.
journal: Theory and Practice in Language Studies

title: The Authorial Image and Stylization in Contemporary (2012-2023) Kazakh Short Stories: A Linguostylistic Analysis
abstract: In linguistic analysis, literary discourse is regarded as a domain that reveals the developmental potential and trajectory of a national language. An author’s style is not merely a reflection of the use of established linguistic norms; rather, it functions as an influential model that revitalizes, consolidates, or transforms those norms. Through lexical choice, syntagmatic construction, the conventionalization of figurative units, and the formation of new semantic nuances, a literary text actively affects the normative character of the national language. The article examines the construction of the authorial image and the mechanisms of stylization in contemporary Kazakh short stories, drawing on the linguostylistic analysis model developed by Rabiga Syzdyk. In accordance with the theoretical framework of the study, the authorial image is not equal with the writer’s biographical persona; instead, it is conceptualized as a category reconstructed from the internal organization of the text, narrative perspectives, evaluative and modal nuances, and the dominant use of expressive means. The empirical corpus of this research consists of Kazakh short stories published between 2012 and 2023. The texts were selected from Qazaq adebieti and other literary portals and were analyzed regarding their intrageneric differentiation (psychological, philosophical, allegorical, mystical, socio-domestic, etc.). The article contributes to the development of studies on the authorial image, stylization, and the transformation of stylistic norms by introducing materials from the Turkic languages into international scholarly discourse.
journal: Theory and Practice in Language Studies

title: Adoption of Improved Pigeonpea (Cajanus cajan) Production Technologies in India-Status, Constraints and Opportunities: A Review
abstract: Pigeonpea (Cajanus cajan L.) is a major pulse crop of India, contributing significantly to protein security and soil fertility in rainfed dryland systems. Despite the development of several improved production technologies, their adoption among smallholder farmers remains partial and uneven. A comprehensive literature search was conducted using Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar and Science Direct. Studies published between 2000 and 2024 and focusing on pigeonpea production technologies and technology adoption were considered. After screening for relevance, peer-reviewed articles, reports from ICAR, ICRISAT and FAO and government publications were synthesized in this narrative review. India accounts for approximately 70 per cent of global pigeonpea area and production, yet national average productivity remains below 900 kg/ha - well short of the attainable yield potential. Adoption of improved varieties and recommended agronomic practices is hampered by non-availability of quality seeds, high pest and disease pressure, price fluctuations, labour shortages, climatic risks and inadequate extension outreach. Socio-economic factors - including education, farm size, institutional access and economic incentives - significantly determine adoption behaviour. Site-level evidence indicates that adoption of improved varieties can reach roughly 90 per cent of cropped area where active seed-multiplication support is present, against a considerably lower and uneven baseline elsewhere, while national productivity grew at only about -1.7 per cent per annum over 2016-17 to 2021-22, underscoring a yield gap driven more by uneven technology diffusion than by area constraints. Emerging opportunities include hybrid and climate-resilient varieties, digital advisory platforms, Farmer producer organizations (FPOs) and climate-smart agriculture practices that can collectively narrow yield gaps and improve farm income.

title: UNMANNED AERIAL VEHICLES AND THE INTERNET OF THINGS IN AGRICULTURE: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF TECHNOLOGICAL DIRECTIONS AND DEVELOPMENT PROSPECTS
abstract: Relevance. Modern agriculture is undergoing a profound cyber-physical transformation driven by the need to shift from extensive to precision, high-accuracy, and environmentally balanced production methods. The technological foundation of this transition is the integration of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and wireless Internet of Things (IoT) sensor networks, which together form the concept of Agriculture 5.0. Despite the rapid growth of publications on this topic, the accumulated body of research remains fragmented across directions (computer vision, network technologies, robotics, adoption economics), which complicates the formation of a holistic picture of the field and of priority directions for further research. The subject of this study are methods and technologies of applying UAVs and IoT networks to precision-agriculture tasks. The purpose of the article to systematize and classify current scientific research on the use of UAVs and IoT in agriculture, and to determine the leading technological directions, their quantitative proportions, and promising development vectors. The following results were obtained. A total of 198 scientific publications from 2024-2026 were processed and classified into seven thematic classes: crop health and biological threat monitoring, hardware engineering, edge computing and spraying, navigation, swarm intelligence and data collection, phenotyping, biomass and yield forecasting, soil science, water balance and precision irrigation, economics, ecology and socio-cultural perception, and specialized agrotechnical operations. For each class, consolidated tables of applied methods and results, as well as diagrams revealing the internal structure of the direction, were constructed. The dominance of navigation/swarm-control tasks and biological-threat monitoring was identified, along with key technical barriers (limited battery energy density, beyond-visual-line-of-sight flight regulations, and fragmentation of data-exchange standards). Conclusion. The obtained results provide a holistic assessment of the state and structure of the research field on UAV and IoT applications in agriculture and can serve as a basis for shaping further research programs and educational courses in precision agriculture. Future research directions concern improving the energy autonomy of platforms, standardizing data-exchange protocols, and developing edge artificial-intelligence models resilient to complex field conditions.

title: Being Granular, Becoming Sustainable:
abstract: This article examines the integration of digitization and environmental concerns in digital agriculture from the perspective of actors in smart farming in Switzerland. Those actors, previously unconnected to farming, promote the use of granular data to achieve more sustainable practices. Considering granularity as a practitioner-made achievement rather than a technical property alone, I draw on interviews and ethnographic observations, and rely on material-semiotic insights from STS (Law, 2008; Mol, 1999; Lien & Law, 2011) to examine how granularity data is brought into existence through heterogeneous practices. I first analyze how the connection between digital agriculture and more sustainable practices is operated as a motto, an aspirational principle that draws from different sources and comparisons. I then show how the production and interpretation of granular data depend on experimental infrastructures, interdisciplinary collaboration, and ongoing human interpretation, all of which contribute to the existence of granularity while enacting specific definitions of sustainability.

title: Morphological Trait-based Prediction of Konjac (Amorphophallus muelleri Blume) Corm Yield Across Mother Corm Sizes Under Shaded and Potassium-fertilized Conditions
abstract: Konjac ( Amorphophallus muelleri Blume) is a tuberous crop grown for its glucomannan-rich corms, but yield determinants under semi-intensive production remain poorly understood. This study aimed to identify size-specific morphological traits that could serve as indicators of corm yield of A. muelleri and to determine the growth stage at which these traits showed the strongest relationships with final yield. A factorial field experiment was conducted using two mother corm size classes (small and large) and four potassium (K) fertilization rates (0, 75, 150 and 225 kg K/ha) under 70% shade. Non-destructive and destructive measurements of root and shoot traits were taken at 12 and 18 weeks after planting (WAP), and simple linear regression analyses were conducted separately for each corm-size class to examine the relationships between selected vegetative traits and final corm yield. Adjusted coefficients of determination for the strongest fitted relationships ranged from 0.42 to 0.71. In plants derived from small mother corms, Root Fresh Weight (RFW) at 18 WAP showed the strongest association with yield, represented by the regression equation: Yield (t/ha) = 0.25 × RFW (g/plant) + 38.49 (adjusted R 2 = 0.43). In plants derived from large mother corms, Petiole Fresh Weight (PFW) showed the strongest association with yield. The relationship at 12 WAP explained more variation in yield than that at 18 WAP and was represented by the regression equation: Yield (t/ha) = 0.08 × PFW (g/plant) + 33.98 (adjusted R 2 = 0.71). The contrasting trait-yield relationships suggest different physiological limitations between corm sizes, with yield in small-corm plants being more closely linked to belowground establishment and resource acquisition, whereas in large-corm plants it is more influenced by canopy development and assimilate supply. Final corm yield of A. muelleri was most strongly associated with RFW in plants derived from small mother corms and with PFW in plants derived from large mother corms. The strongest relationship was observed between PFW at 12 WAP and final yield in large-corm plants. These equations should be interpreted as exploratory, condition-specific trait–yield relationships rather than validated prediction models. Because they were derived from a single-location, single-season experiment conducted under 70% shade and a fixed management system, validation across locations, seasons, shade levels, and management practices is required before any predictive application.

title: X-River: A Differentiable Saint-Venant River Routing Framework for Efficient Spatial Parameter Learning and Hybrid Hydrological Modeling
abstract: Accurate large-scale streamflow simulation relies on river routing models, which are highly biased as their parameters remain poorly constrained. Traditional calibration methods become computationally intractable as parameter dimensionality and spatial resolution grow. Differentiable modeling offers a path forward, but to the best of our knowledge, no existing differentiable model spatially solves the full dynamics of one-dimensional (1D) Saint-Venant Equations (SVE). Here we present X-River, a differentiable, spatially distributed river routing model that solves the 1D SVE using JAX, a framework that natively supports automatic differentiation. X-River implements both a full dynamic wave solver and a kinematic wave approximation, with the latter being substantially faster in backward pass. When driven by a pre-simulated runoff forcing in the Delaware River Basin, X-River reproduces daily streamflow with comparable performance to a widely used routing model. Its differentiability enables gradient-based calibration that is orders of magnitude more efficient than perturbation-based methods and scales to spatially distributed parameters, yielding physically consistent parameter fields. We further couple X-River with a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network designed for generating runoff at the grid level. The hybrid framework substantially improves daily streamflow and generalizes to ungauged reaches better than a lumped LSTM setup. This is because the hybrid framework enables end-to-end learning from sparse gauges to every upstream cell through river network backpropagation. By making a physically based SVE routing model fully differentiable, X-River opens a pathway to couple with differentiable land models for parameter learning and to support accurate hydrological simulation at large scales.
