title: Shaping maternal physiology: Immune control of reproductive adaptation
abstract: Pregnancy is one of the most extensive physiological transitions of adult life, requiring coordinated adaptation across virtually every maternal organ to support fetal growth while preserving maternal health. Although these changes have traditionally been viewed as endocrine driven, emerging evidence identifies the immune system as an active regulator of maternal physiology. The immune system is increasingly recognized as a broad regulator of host physiology, positioning it as a key driver of maternal adaptation. In this work, we discuss how pregnancy reprograms maternal immunity to orchestrate physiological reprograming of tissues. This framework shifts the view of maternal immunity from one centered on immune homeostasis and fetal tolerance to one in which immune cells actively instruct physiological short- and long-term adaptation across maternal organs to shape health beyond reproduction.

title: Sex-specific mechanisms of chronic pain
abstract: For decades, we have known that women, especially younger women, are disproportionately affected by pain disorders, including irritable bowel syndrome, endometriosis, menstrual migraines, fibromyalgia, osteoarthritis, and neuropathic pain, all of which degrade quality of life. The adoption of sex as a biological variable in 2016 has begun to transform the field, revealing distinct sex-specific pathways that initiate, amplify, and resolve pain. In this Review, we synthesize recent advances across visceral and somatic pain, highlighting the impact of sex hormones, immune-neural cross-talk, the gut microbiome, and endogenous analgesic circuits. Rather than clinging to the historical standard that simply described the female bias in pain symptoms, these studies begin to explain why females experience heightened pain, paving the path for mechanism-based precision therapeutics.

title: Keep AI-augmented science contestable
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is moving upstream in science. Systems such as AlphaFold have already transformed protein-structure prediction, while newer agentic systems can search literatures, generate hypotheses, write and execute code, interpret results, and automate much of the path from idea to paper. Recent debates have asked how such systems may change scientific progress, surprise, and human understanding. Yet they also change something more fundamental: who—or what—participates in deciding which questions are asked, which evidence is surfaced, and which alternatives survive. As machine intelligence becomes part of science’s epistemic infrastructure, steps must be taken to ensure that researchers who did not build, own, or operate the system can still contest how ideas and evidence became a claim.

AutoCodeSherpa: Symbolic Explanations in AI Coding Agents
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents integrate external tools with one or more LLMs to accomplish specific tasks. Agents have rapidly been adopted by developers, and they are starting to be deployed in industrial workflows, such as their use to fix static analysis issues from the widely used SonarQube static analyzer. However, the growing importance of agents means their actions carry greater impact and potential risk. Thus, to use them at scale, an additional layer of trust and evidence is necessary. This work presents AutoCodeSherpa, a technique that provides explanations of software issues in the form of symbolic formulae. Inspired by the reachability, infection, and propagation model of software faults, the explanations are composed of input, infection, and output conditions, collectively providing a specification of the issue. In practice, the symbolic explanation is implemented as a combination of a property-based test (PBT) and program-internal symbolic expressions. Critically, this means our symbolic explanations are executable and can be automatically evaluated, unlike natural language explanations. Experiments show the generated conditions are highly accurate. For example, input conditions from AutoCodeSherpa had an accuracy of 85.7%. This high accuracy makes symbolic explanations particularly useful in two scenarios. First, the explanations can be used in automated issue resolution environments to decide whether to accept or reject patches from issue resolution agents; AutoCodeSherpa could reject 2x as many incorrect patches as baselines did. Second, as agentic AI approaches continue to develop, program analysis driven explanations like ours can be provided to other LLM-based repair techniques which do not employ analysis to improve their output. In our experiments, our symbolic explanations could improve the plausible patch generation rate of the Agentless technique by 60%.

title: AgentInspect: Diagnosing Behavioral Failures in Artificial Intelligence Agents
abstract: Effectively testing Artificial Intelligence (AI) agents remains a fundamental challenge due to their stochastic reasoning, vast and diverse input space, reliance on external tools, and operation in dynamic execution environments; factors that demand new testing methodologies explicitly tailored to the complex and interactive nature of agent-based systems. This work presents a novel methodology for testing AI agents, with a particular focus on assessing their behavioral robustness under varied operational conditions. Our approach relies on following key technical innovations: (1) a coverage-guided test input generation strategy based on agent- specific coverage objectives, (2) a capture-and-simulate mechanism that systematically emulates abnormal tool behaviors to mimic real-world execution failures, and (3) a deterministic behavioral failure detection approach that enables consistent identification of failures across different test inputs. We developed AgentInspect, a framework that automatically detects six types of behavioral failures in LangChain-based AI agents by analyzing their execution trajectories across three evaluation settings: a baseline setting using real tool responses, a simulated setting incorporating synthetic tool responses, and a hybrid setting that combines the real and simulated tool responses. To evaluate our approach, we curated a benchmark of 35 AI agents obtained from GitHub. Our results show that AgentInspect consistently identifies different behavioral failures with high precision and recall across all three execution settings. In particular, the simulated and hybrid settings expose failure modes that do not emerge during baseline execution with real tool responses, thereby enabling a more comprehensive assessment of agent robustness. Our findings highlight AgentInspect’s effectiveness in revealing critical failures and its practical utility for systematic robustness evaluation of AI agents.
journal: Proceedings of the ACM on Software Engineering

title: SPONGE: Adaptive Boundary-Anchored Indexing for Online Value-Flow Queries
abstract: The application of high-precision value-flow analysis is experiencing a paradigm shift from planned executions to online ad hoc queries driven by human auditors and AI agents. However, existing techniques struggle in this interactive setting: exhaustive offline tabulation is fundamentally intractable, while memoryless online search suffers from redundant exploration and SMT invocations. To bridge this gap, we propose SPONGE, a novel two-phase framework that accelerates ad hoc queries through boundary-anchored indexing. Offline, SPONGE employs an adaptive-depth strategy to selectively precompute feasible value-flow segments at critical procedure boundaries, optimizing SMT allocation based on traversal probability and search space complexity. Online, it utilizes an index-guided push-down search with lazy expansion to dynamically stitch these pre-verified segments, effectively bypassing redundant state exploration and pruning unsatisfiable paths. We evaluated SPONGE on 9 C/C++ projects (up to 3.8 million LoC). Results demonstrate that SPONGE drops the 95th-percentile online query time from nearly 270 s to under 50 s compared to a baseline search. Furthermore, the adaptive strategy reduces offline indexing time by 75% over a uniform approach, amortizing the offline cost in fewer than 300 queries for workloads dominated by complex queries.
journal: Proceedings of the ACM on Programming Languages

title: Croquetify: Transforming Single-User Functional Reactive Programs into Multi-user Applications
abstract: Building robust real-time collaborative applications --- "multi-user apps" --- is hard. State transitions that are trivial in the single-user case become surprisingly complex once concurrent participants are involved, often requiring custom interaction protocols and tailor-made speculative execution and reconciliation mechanisms. Errors are harder to reproduce, and the application must still respond within milliseconds. AI coding agents do not yet handle these demands reliably. In this paper, we present a novel way to develop multi-user apps. We employ a combination of a Functional Reactive Programming language called Renkon, which is a general-purpose language for application development with rich meta-programming features, and a network application framework called Croquet. We devised a program transformation that allows the same Renkon program to run as a single-user app or to use Croquet to run as a multi-user app without writing application-specific server-side code. This is done without losing Renkon's live programming capability. To demonstrate how well this approach works for a practical application, we applied it to a real-time interactive programming environment called Renkon-pad. We show that not only can we transform a single-user programming environment into a multi-user one, but also that the multi-user environment can be used to develop a multi-user app in a live programming manner. This experiment supports the idea that the transformation is applicable to general and complex programs, with the programmers' intent in the original program preserved.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM SIGPLAN International Symposium on New Ideas, New Paradigms, and Reflections on Programming and Software

title: The Developer as Curator: A Canvas for Coding Agent Context
abstract: The quality of AI-generated code depends on the context that coding agents automatically receive as input. Today's coding agents do not expose that context to the developer. When retrieval fails, the developer cannot distinguish whether a wrong output stems from flawed reasoning or from incorrect or missing input. We describe how coding agents retrieve context internally and derive three failure modes: wrong context, missing context and stale context. Existing mechanisms for managing context (compaction, session reset, and sub-agent delegation) are automated responses to token limits that give developers no way to correct these failures. We present Monet, a canvas-based development tool that positions the developer as curator of the context the agent receives. Monet is guided by two design goals: context observability, letting developers see every piece of gathered context and its current state, and context curation, letting developers add, remove, and refresh context through direct manipulation. On Monet's canvas, each piece of context is a node that developers can remove, add, or refresh to correct the agent's input before re-prompting. Case studies show that each mechanism catches retrieval errors that autonomous agents cannot self-correct. Monet opens a new design space for human-AI collaboration in agent-assisted programming, shifting the developer's role from prompt author to context curator.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM SIGPLAN International Symposium on New Ideas, New Paradigms, and Reflections on Programming and Software

title: Leveraging vision language models for digit recognition on digital measuring devices: a comparative analysis
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) with multimodal input capability have been demonstrated in various applications. Vision language models (VLMs), which were developed from LLMs, can process and learn both visual and textual data simultaneously, enabling them to generate descriptive text from images. This study explores the use of several VLM models for the seven-segment digit recognition of a digital measuring device compared with other baseline optical character recognition (OCR) methods, such as Tesseract OCR, EasyOCR, PaddleOCR, KerasOCR, and YOLO11, with or without the integration of you only look once 11 (YOLO11) for LCD screen cropping. The results showed that the Gemini model outperformed conventional OCR methods and other VLM models with an average per-digit-recognition (PDR) accuracy of 98.10% (?=0.36%) and full sequence reading (FSR) accuracy of 93.85% (?=1.29%). The performance evaluation across the distance variation also demonstrates high accuracy for the VLM result with stable results. Simultaneously, YOLO11 exhibits degradation at longer distances due to difficulty in detecting small decimal digits, whereas the traditional OCR method yields inconsistent results. This study showed promising results for the further development, improvement, and deployment of VLM models in the automatic seven-segment digit recognition task on the edge device.
journal: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics

title: Hybrid multi-task deep learning framework for joint forecasting of solar and wind power
abstract: This study presents the adaptive three-expert ensemble (A3E), a reproducible framework for joint one-hour-ahead solar and wind power forecasting. A3E combines temporal, physically informed, and high-generation Extra Trees experts through a causal local-error gate and is evaluated under a strictly chronological, leakage-free protocol. After timestamp reconciliation and causal feature construction, the primary source yielded 8,700 model-ready observations: 5,775 for training, 1,463 for validation, 719 for internal testing, and 743 for a same-source December holdout. The primary scale-neutral comparison used Macro train-SD normalized root mean square error (NRMSE) on 672 common forecast origins. A3E achieved 0.1978, compared with 0.2314 for the official photovoltaic (PV)-Client 2026 comparator and 0.2340 for TimeMixer. However, validation-optimized static weights achieved 0.2017 on the complete 719-origin internal test, compared with 0.2025 for adaptive A3E; the difference was not statistically significant under dependence-aware analysis. On the independent CISO and ERCO systems, TimeMixer outperformed A3E, demonstrating source-dependent model rankings. Event evaluation used 98 CISO and 320 ERCO high-generation events. The results support the value of heterogeneous expert integration, but not a universal accuracy advantage of adaptive weighting.
journal: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics

title: Automated system with ESP32 for monitoring vertical hydroponic farming and air quality
abstract: Urban population growth has increased air pollution levels and adversely affected public health, highlighting the need for sustainable solutions in densely populated cities. While urban agriculture and monitoring technologies offer alternatives for improving the climate, there is limited integration of automated systems to optimize hydroponic vertical farming. Research shows that urban agriculture and vertical hydroponic farming contribute to improving the urban climate through the integration of sensors and intelligent control models. This research proposes a low-cost automated system based on ESP32 for hydroponic crops and environmental monitoring, integrating sensors, actuators, and threshold-based control algorithms with wireless connectivity to regulate agro-environmental variables. A cyclical control system is implemented that periodically evaluates variables such as temperature, substrate moisture, pH, and turbidity with configurable thresholds, automatically activating actuators to maintain optimal growing conditions. The results show that automated irrigation control, real-time monitoring, and CO2 reduction were achieved under controlled conditions, demonstrating its usefulness for environmental management. Future work proposes integrating predictive algorithms with automatic alerts.
journal: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics

title: CLARA: a unified hybrid ai-human receptionist framework using WebRTC and Monorepo architecture
abstract: The rapid digitalization of enterprise infrastructure has caused a major change in institutional communication. This change requires the traditional front desk to transform into a high-tech center for security and logistics. However, current automated solutions often create what is known as the “automation paradox.” In this situation, removing human oversight increases the importance and complexity of the remaining interactions. This work outlines the design, implementation, and evaluation of conversational low-latency AI receptionist agent (CLARA). CLARA is a new hybrid system which solves the problems of unattended kiosks by combining a conversational AI, which uses the Google Gemini API, with a low-latency, real-time WebRTC video calling system. The design features a strong 3-Tier Monorepo built with React, TypeScript, Express.js, Socket.IO, and PostgreSQL. This setup ensures type safety and consistency in the code across the entire stack. Key contributions of this project include a custom Socket.IO signaling server for secure peer-to-peer connections, a “Human-in-the-Loop” workflow that reduces handoff issues, and an “Offline-First” strategy ensuring the system keeps working during network disruptions. Performance tests show that CLARA achieves less than 200 ms glass-to-glass latency and handles high traffic well, proving it is an effective and reliable solution for modern visitor management.
journal: International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering (IJECE)

title: Plant disease classification using lightweight deep learning architectures
abstract: Detecting early-stage pathogens of plant diseases is a challenging task due to the low pathogen density and the subtlety or absence of visible symptoms. If not identified at an early stage, plant diseases can progress rapidly, making them significantly harder to control. Therefore, real-time and in-situ monitoring of plants is essential for tracking diseases and enabling early intervention. Within the scope of smart agriculture applications, crop health can be assessed and productivity can be maintained through mobile devices. In this study, the performance of lightweight neural network architectures on various plant disease datasets was compared, targeting devices with limited memory resources such as mobile devices and embedded systems, which we consider potential candidates for edge deployment based on the measured accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. The architectures evaluated include SqueezeNet, MobileViT, EdgeNeXt, GhostNet, EfficientNet, and LeViT. The plant datasets used in the experiments were Plant Disease, Cassava, and Turmeric. Each model was evaluated using Accuracy, F1-Score, Precision, and Recall metrics. Among the three datasets, the best performance was achieved on the Turmeric dataset using the GhostNet architecture, with scores of 0.9978 (Accuracy), 0.9976 (F1-Score), 0.9976 (Precision), and 0.9976 (Recall), respectively.
journal: Journal of Intelligent & Fuzzy Systems: Applications in Engineering and Technology

title: Bi-temporal LiDAR-based estimates of stand variables reduce growth modelling costs in even-aged Larix olgensis A. Henry plantations
abstract: We developed a dynamic stand-level growth and yield model using bi-temporal UAV LiDAR data to support forest management and planning. This approach aims to reduce the cost and intensity of ground-based inventories by using low-cost UAV LiDAR as an alternative data source. Growth and yield models, as the principal tools for simulating and forecasting stand development dynamics, support sustainable long-term planning of forest resource management. This study developed a dynamic growth model for even-aged tree stands based on bi-temporal field measurements and UAV LiDAR data, using Larix olgensis A. Henry—a common afforestation species in Northeast China—as the focal species. The field measurements and the LiDAR scans were done in 2019 and 2023. We evaluated the suitability of using LiDAR-based estimates for stand variables (stand age, dominant height, basal area and number of trees per hectare) as modeling data. Models based on field measurements provided the benchmark. The growth and yield models consisted of three simultaneously fitted equations: the first for the dominant height, the second for the number of trees per hectare, and the third for the stand basal area. The LiDAR-predicted values of the variables were obtained by using the k‑nearest‑neighbors (kNN) imputation method. Models based on LiDAR-estimated stand variables were very similar to those based on field measurements. The models were used to simulate stand development from 2019 to 2023, using either field data or LiDAR-based variables as predictors. The simulation results for dominant height were the best when both the models and the inventory data consisted of LiDAR-based estimates. For the stand basal area and number of trees, the field inventory yielded better simulation results than using LiDAR estimates in the area-based inventory approach. The results indicated that predicted LiDAR-based variables can be used to develop stand-level growth and yield models for plantation forests, in addition to using LiDAR in forest inventory.

title: Machine learning analysis of land use change dynamics in Malawi’s Chia Lagoon
abstract: Land-use and land-cover (LULC) change is a major driver of ecosystem degradation, particularly in freshwater wetlands where spatially explicit evidence is limited. This study aimed to quantify two decades (2004–2024) of LULC change in Malawi’s Chia Lagoon catchment using machine-learning-based remote sensing approaches. Multi-temporal Landsat imagery (2004, 2014, and 2024) was classified using a Random Forest supervised classification algorithm. LULC changes were assessed using three classes (water, vegetation, and bare land), supported by NDVI and MNDWI analyses. Classification accuracy was evaluated using confusion matrices, overall accuracy, producer’s accuracy, and user’s accuracy, with area estimates adjusted using 95% confidence intervals. Following validation of the final confusion matrices, the Random Forest classifications achieved year-specific overall accuracies of 82.0%, 90.%, and 96.0% for 2004, 2014, and 2024, respectively. Between 2004 and 2024, mapped vegetation decreased from 519 km² (15.4%) to 330 km² (9.8%), representing a net decrease of 189 km² and 5.6% points in catchment share. Bare land increased by 208 km² (+ 6.2% points), whereas mapped water decreased by approximately 20 km² (− 0.6% points). NDVI and MNDWI provided complementary spectral information for interpreting vegetation greenness and surface-water patterns but were not treated as independent validation of the classified area changes. The classified Landsat record indicates significant changes in land-cover composition between 2004 and 2024, including a net reduction in mapped vegetation and a net increase in non-vegetated surfaces, despite a partial increase in vegetation between 2014 and 2024. Because the analysis is based on three dry-season observations and a broad three-class classification scheme, the results should be interpreted as mapped land-cover changes rather than direct evidence of specific causal processes or ecological degradation. Machine-learning-supported remote sensing provides a useful framework for identifying landscape changes that can subsequently be investigated through targeted field-based monitoring.” Not applicable.

title: Growth regularities and dry organic biomass accumulation rates in drip-irrigated tomato under different soil watering thresholds
abstract: This study established the regularities of dry organic matter accumulation throughout the growth period of drip-irrigated tomato ( Solanum lycopersicum L.), cultivated in the cold semi-arid climate zone (BSk), under various watering thresholds using a logistic function. The proposed mathematical models closely matched the empirical data, yielding strong coefficients of determination (R 2 of 0.98). Growth parameter modeling demonstrated that maintaining a soil moisture threshold in the layer 0–50 cm of at least 70% field capacity (FC) from seedlings planting to bud - ding, followed by 80% FC during peak growth intensity, optimizes biomass accumulation dynamics. The absolute highest dry organic matter accumulation rate (0.623 t ha -1 day -1 ) was recorded at the critical curve inflection point (T 2 ) under a dynamic 70–80–70% FC irrigation regime. Peak growth acceleration (0.024 t ha -1 day -2 ) occurred at critical point T 1 . The intensive growth phase terminated upon reaching critical point T 3 , transitioning into a deceleration phase characterized by negative acceleration values, which temporally coincided with intensive fruit formation. The duration of this intensive growth window varied from 13.2 to 19.1 days depending on moisture availability. Ultimately, maintaining soil moisture below 70% FC or exceeding 80% FC is agronomically impractical because these moisture extremes significantly depress both growth rate and acceleration, reducing overall crop productivity.

title: Mineral supplements improve the nutritional value of forage and the livestock carrying capacity of high-Andean pastures
abstract: This study evaluated the effects of calcium-based soil amendments and pasture composition on forage produc - tivity, nutritional quality, and livestock carrying capacity in high-Andean grassland systems. A field experiment was analyzed using linear mixed-effects models to assess the effects of soil amendments (limestone, dolomite, and gypsum), pasture types ( Lolium multiflorum , Trifolium pratense , and their mixture), and their interaction on productivity, nutritional composition, derived nutritional indicators, and feed-related performance. Soil amendments significantly increased forage productivity and feed availability, improving dry matter production, crude protein yield, energy yield, and livestock carrying capacity. Limestone and gypsum showed the most consistent positive effects across productivity-related variables. Pasture composition mainly influenced forage nutritional quality. Trifolium pratense increased crude protein concentration, protein-derived energy, and protein: fiber ratio, while Lolium multiflorum showed higher fiber and carbohydrate concentrations. Mixed pastures exhibited intermediate values, reflecting functional complementarity between species. Although total energy concentra - tion remained unaffected by treatments, calcium-based amendments increased the proportion of protein-derived energy, improving the nutritional efficiency of the forage. Multivariate analysis confirmed clear differentiation between amended and non-amended systems, with legumes associated with improved nutritional quality and productivity-related indicators. In conclusion, calcium-based soil amendments enhance forage production and feed availability, while legume inclusion improves forage protein value. The combined use of soil fertility management and pasture diversification represents an effective strategy to improve feed resources and livestock production efficiency in high-Andean systems.

title: Authoritarian AI’s Last-Mile Problem
abstract: Is artificial intelligence the autocrats’ silver bullet? No. AI-empowered autocrats are constrained by the “last-mile problem”: AI can help regimes to see, sort, and predict, but human police officers, soldiers, and local officials remain indispensable for physical coercion. In the long run, human agents will stay relevant: They not only guarantee an effective repressive system but also signal the autocrats’ popularity. For prodemocracy actors, this suggests that the conventional wisdom on combating autocracies, such as encouraging defections among security forces, still holds. The bottom line: Repression in the AI era remains a human affair.

title: Informed forecasting: Leveraging auxiliary knowledge to boost large language model performance on time series forecasting
abstract: The rapid adoption of large language models (LLMs) has sparked growing interest in extending their capabilities beyond traditional natural language tasks, including applications in time series forecasting. This work explores the enhancement of time series forecasting with LLMs by incorporating time-dependent covariates. We propose a set of representative prompting strategies that span a wide range of formats while incorporating covariates, and then implement the proposed framework to evaluate performance across three real-world time series datasets in healthcare, service operations, and transportation. In our experiments, we use GPT-4o-mini and show that incorporating relevant covariate information through an appropriate prompt design can substantially improve forecasting accuracy, reducing prediction errors by up to 70% compared with the no-covariate baseline. Furthermore, the analysis reveals that both the choice of covariate and the prompt structure are critical, as poorly aligned configurations may degrade performance. Finally, we conduct sensitivity analyses to assess the effect of covariate integration in censored settings and quantify uncertainty, confirming that our method achieves statistically significant improvements over existing approaches. These findings underscore the potential of covariate integration in prompt design to bridge the gap between general-purpose LLMs and forecasting tasks.

title: Measure of Emotional Episodes with Music (MEEM): Development and psychometric evaluation of a modular instrument
abstract: Emotional episodes experienced with music are embedded within the milieu of everyday life, yet most existing psychometric instruments only capture trait-like tendencies rather than state-like contextual factors. In this article, we detail the development of the Measure of Emotional Episodes with Music (MEEM) as a modular solution to capture situational and contextual dimensions of music-related emotional experiences. Building upon prior content-validity evaluation and grounded in the Episode Model, we tested the hypothesised dimensionality for the five constructs across two online vignette experiments. Evaluative confirmatory factor analyses (CFA) in the first experiment supported the assumed latent structure for each of five constructs, showing good model fit and clear differentiation among sub-constructs. Several sub-constructs were refined to more aptly reflect the specific facets captured by the best-performing items. Taking a three item model for each construct forward into a second experiment, CFA again supported the first experiment results and the original hypothesised structure. Associations between the five MEEM scales and two types of emotion ratings (HAAS and GEMIAC) were gathered as an initial indicator of convergent validity. Analysis of a factor structure combining all five constructs did not favour a hierarchical model specified by a single higher-order latent factor but instead a multidimensional interpretation, consistent with Episode Model assumptions. MEEM consists of five separate scales, each representing a theoretically derived construct—with two or three sub-constructs—measured with 35 items in total. Concurrent but distinct development of five constructs permits individualised applications for each of the five scales. This modular design of MEEM allows researchers to administer either the full battery or selected scales depending on their research aims. By targeting emotional states as dynamic, situated, and functionally grounded processes, MEEM provides a meaningful alternative to trait-based instruments, and offers a foundation for future validation and cross-contextual applications.

title: Using GIS, remote-sensing and linear modeling to prioritize spatially explicit action against erosion and sediment transport within Lake Victoria watershed in Kenya
abstract: Watershed degradation from human encroachment is a worldwide phenomenon and a keystone driver of erosion, transport and deposition of sediment material into downstream lakes and other water bodies. Despite global recognition of the growing scale of these linkages, comprehensive evaluation and ranking of the range of specific parameters associated catchment destruction and subsequent sediment movement, or those contributing to its mitigation, has rarely been undertaken. This study applied GIS with remote-sensing with linear modeling to assess influence of geomorphic and hydrological as well as land-use land-cover (LULC) elements in driving net erosion indicator (NEI), sediment transport indices (STI), and an index of overall erosion potential, ErPot combining NEI and STI. The LULCs were: crop cover, forest cover, wetland cover, urban-features cover while the geomorphic-hydrological parameters were slope gradient, elevation and sub-watershed size. This was undertaken across 10 delineated sub-watersheds forming the catchment of Lake Victoria on the Kenyan territory side. NEI was predicted to be enhanced by cop cover, urban development and slope angle; STI was enhanced by slope angle, sub-watershed upslope size. While ErPot increased with sub-watershed upslope size, NEI, STI and ErPot were all predicted to be mitigated by forest and wetland cover sizes. Using these results, the sub-watersheds of Busia-North, Rangwe and Homabay-North were considered priority for action to reduce net erosion indicator. Similarly, the Mara and Yala sub-catchments, and also the Mara the Yala and Nzoia sub-catchments were considered of greatest significance in prioritizing action to mitigate sediment transport and overall erosivity, respectively. These results, the first from modeling a trans-boundary freshwater catchment erosion, are practically applicable in decision making for designing a county-based strategy for habitat rehabilitation and conservation that specifically prioritizes the critical zones identified.

title: Potential flood hazard analysis in paddy field: A case study in part of Kedungbener Subwatershed, Kebumen Regency, Indonesia
abstract: The high flood hazard potential in the Kedungbener Subwatershed significantly impacts the surrounding environment, including the agricultural sector. This research aimed to analyze potential flood hazards to agricultural areas under 2-year and 10-year return period scenarios. Flood hazard was generated using HEC-RAS with a rain-on-grid approach to identify the distribution and extent of the inundation area over land cover. The results demonstrated that the flood-affected agricultural areas reached 921.15 ha (58.12%) for the 2-year return period and 994.47 ha (62.75%) for the 10-year return period. This indicates that more than half of the agricultural areas were impacted by the flood. The model was validated using a confusion matrix, which showed that the under-2-year return period flood model achieved an accuracy of 84.38%, while the 10-year return period flood model achieved an accuracy of 90.62%. Given the higher accuracy of the 10-year return period, the model is considered more representative in predicting flood hazards within agricultural areas. Based on that accuracy, the AUC of 0.863 indicates that the HEC-RAS flood hazard prediction model falls within the “Accepted” category. This result provides a critical foundation for the related stakeholders to formulate targeted flood mitigation strategies for the agricultural sector.
journal: Journal of Degraded and Mining Lands Management

title: Carbon storage in Inga-cacao agroforestry on degraded former coca-crop soils
abstract: Former coca-crop lands in the Peruvian Amazon need restoration that rebuilds soil function and carbon pools. This study compared soil, litter and recovered-root carbon in degraded former coca-crop soil without agroforestry and Inga edulis-Theobroma cacao systems aged 2, 4 and 6 years. Three blocks provided 12 sampling units of 100 m². Soil carbon (0–20 cm) used organic matter and bulk density; litter and roots were sampled in 0.25 m² quadrats. Block-adjusted analysis and exact within-block tests detected condition effects for all pools after false-discovery-rate adjustment (adjusted P = 0.0069-0.0330). Total carbon was 13.06 ± 2.34 t C ha?¹ without agroforestry and 48.06 ± 3.44, 62.62 ± 3.87 and 59.77 ± 5.86 t C ha?¹ in the 2-, 4- and 6-year systems, respectively. A parallel first-order compartment model fitted the three pools and derived total carbon as their sum. The derived total curve had R² = 0.921 and a model-implied asymptote of 65.88 t C ha?¹; apparent response coefficients were 0.857 yr?¹ for soil, 0.387 yr?¹ for litter and 0.242 yr?¹ for roots. Agroforestry conditions contained more measured carbon than the non-agroforestry condition, but total carbon did not differ among agroforestry ages. The fitted coefficients describe a cross-sectional condition-age gradient rather than measured annual sequestration. Estimates exclude aboveground biomass and soil below 20 cm.
journal: Journal of Degraded and Mining Lands Management

title: Automated Landslide Scar Detection in the Himalayan Region Using Satellite Imagery and YOLO-Based Deep Learning Models
abstract: Landslides in the Himalayan region are the most serious hazards due to their destructive consequences in the context of life and the economy. More landslides are anticipated based on the present environmental and climatic scenario. Hence, a landslide information detection model is the foremost for hazard risk assessment. The application of deep learning algorithms in hazard analysis has gained significant attention worldwide. Moreover, remote sensing technology has emerged as a critical tool in diverse applications. Therefore, this study leverages the recent scientific and technological developments for extracting landslide-related information. We applied four YOLO (You Only Look Once) models, specifically YOLOv5, YOLOv6, YOLOv7, and YOLOv8, alongside eleven additional YOLO variants to detect landslide scars from satellite imagery. The study focuses on the Greater Himalayan Range, Nepal, utilising a dataset of 275 satellite images, divided into training, validation, and testing sets. The standard quantitative indicators, i.e., precision, recall, F-score, and mean average precision (mAP), are used for evaluation. The results indicate that YOLOv8 achieved the highest accuracy (F-score: 0.857), followed by YOLOv5, YOLOv7, and YOLOv6. These findings highlight the potential of YOLO-based models for rapid and accurate landslide detection, contributing to efficient hazard assessment and disaster response efforts.
journal: Journal Of The Geological Society Of India

title: Groundwater Potential Zonation of Unchehra Watershed, Central India using AHP, Remote Sensing, and GIS Techniques
abstract: Groundwater is the primary source of domestic and agricultural water in the semi-arid regions of central India. Despite receiving moderate annual rainfall, Unchehra watershed experiences seasonal water shortages, especially during summer, highlighting the need for scientific assessment of groundwater resources. This study delineates groundwater potential zones (GWPZs) in the Unchehra watershed using an integrated Remote Sensing (RS), Geographic Information System (GIS), and Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) approach. Seven major factors influencing groundwater occurrence lineament density, geology, land use and land cover (LULC), drainage density, geomorphology, slope and soil type were considered in the analysis. Spatial thematic layers for these parameters were prepared from satellite imagery and Digital Elevation Model (DEM) data using ArcGIS. The relative importance of each factor and its classes was determined through AHP, providing a systematic weighting scheme for groundwater potential assessment. The weighted layers were integrated to generate a groundwater potential zonation map. The resulting map classified the watershed into five groundwater potential zones: very low, low, moderate, high, and very high. The analysis revealed that 7.88% of the watershed falls under very low potential, while significant portions of the area exhibit moderate (28.07%) to very high (22.61%) groundwater potential. To assess the reliability of the generated model, validation was carried out using 41 randomly selected dug wells and Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. The near-zero Consistency Ratio (CR) confirms the reliability of the AHP weighting scheme, while the Area Under the Curve (AUC) value of 0.763 indicates good predictive accuracy of the groundwater potential model. The identified high and very high groundwater potential zones are suitable for groundwater development and artificial recharge measures such as check dams, percolation tanks, and recharge wells. The integrated RS-GIS-AHP framework developed in this study provides a reliable decision-support tool for groundwater exploration, recharge planning, and sustainable groundwater management in Unchehra watershed and similar hydrogeological settings.
journal: Journal Of The Geological Society Of India

title: Role of Asset Protection Strategies in the Recovery of Productive Assets: Evidence from Nepal’s Earthquake
abstract: More than a decade after Nepal’s 2015 earthquake, empirical research on the recovery of productive assets, such as crops, livestock, and farm infrastructure remains limited. In particular, few studies have examined the effectiveness of various asset protection strategies, such as public aid and political connections, in supporting post-disaster recovery. Similarly, no empirical evidence has explicitly evaluated the adequacy of housing aid in covering reconstruction costs. This study addresses these gaps by investigating three main questions. First, it assesses the current status of asset recovery and examines the key factors, including protective strategies that have contributed to household recovery. Second, it analyzes the convergence patterns in the recovery process. Third, it evaluates whether the Government of Nepal’s housing grant sufficiently covered the costs of rebuilding homes. Using data from 680 rural households across nine earthquake-affected districts, the study applies econometric models to generate evidence-based insights. The results show that characteristics like the household head’s gender, marital status, and caste significantly influence recovery. Although migration, remittances, and borrowing offered limited support, strong ties with locally elected officials played a crucial role in asset restoration. The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted recovery efforts, and the analysis revealed a U-shaped convergence pattern in asset recovery. Importantly, the housing grant covered only about half of the reconstruction cost. These findings highlight the need for customized recovery strategies and robust disaster risk reduction policies to restore livelihoods and enhance resilience.

title: Navigating a Synthetic Visual Health Information Environment: Implications of Photorealistic Generative Artificial Intelligence for Public Health.
Comments: New Horizons, New Challenges: ATCE 2026 Returns to Houston
abstract: It’s that time of year again in Houston. From 21 to 23 October, SPE will host thousands of oil and gas industry professionals at its 102nd Annual Technical Conference and Exhibition (ATCE) at the George R. Brown Convention Center. The theme of this year’s gathering is Exploring New Horizons with Innovative Solutions, which also serves as a call to action. Over the past decade, the industry has undergone tremendous change, and technology has often been central to how it has adapted. Over that span, we experienced the 2014 to 2016 oil price crash, which upended countless companies and led to massive layoffs across the industry. In January 2014, Brent crude traded above $107/bbl. A year later, it had fallen to little more than $50/bbl. The slide continued, and by January 2016 prices had dropped to roughly $32.50/bbl. The 2-year downturn that ushered in the era of “lower for longer” was driven in large part by the technological advances that enabled the rise of the North American shale revolution. Markets ultimately recognized that tight oil had materially altered the global supply picture. Just as the industry regained its footing, prices swung sharply again in 2018. Brent climbed to a 4-year high of about $86/bbl in October before falling to $50/bbl by December. During this downturn, particularly among US tight-oil and -gas producers, capital discipline became the defining business strategy as companies faced renewed pressure to improve returns while controlling spending. The pain was real. US oil and gas companies with significant shale exposure collectively lost nearly 30% of their value, while oilfield service providers saw approximately 40% erased from their market capitalization during the downturn. Few in the industry need to be reminded of the disruption that accompanied the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic that swept the industry off its feet just 1 year later. Economies around the world slowed dramatically. Highways emptied, airports went silent, and supply chains were broken. For those of us in the upstream sector, the market shock produced another seemingly unimaginable event. As Brent crude fell to about $14/bbl in April 2020, the US benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI) briefly traded at negative prices, reaching –$37.63/bbl as storage constraints and market dislocation forced overextended traders to offload positions at almost any cost. But 2 years later, economies reopened and the pandemic receded. Negative oil prices became something of a historical anomaly. Then Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in early 2022 sent energy markets into another period of turmoil, driving Brent crude above $125/bbl. That was 4 years ago. And prices retreated again as the world speculated that we were facing yet another oil glut. At the start of this year, many expected oil prices to settle into a range near $60/bbl. Instead, ongoing geopolitical tensions have once again defied market expectations. With the conflict between the US and Iran stretching out for more than 6 months, both Brent and WTI climbed above $100/bbl in September amid supply disruptions and growing concerns over global inventories. This brief walk down memory lane brings us back to ATCE’s theme this year of new horizons and innovative solutions. Over the past decade, the industry has repeatedly been forced to do more with less. The upside of these painful episodes is that producers today are more efficient than ever before and are generating record levels of production with fewer resources than many would have considered possible only a decade ago. But even as we look at $100/bbl oil prices today, few are cheering for them to go higher. The industry understands there is a breaking point for consumers and that demand destruction tends to have significant and lasting consequences. At ATCE, attendees will hear how some of the world’s leading energy producers are dealing with all this uncertainty, which many consider to be a hallmark of our new normal. Discussions will also address the industry’s effort to decarbonize while still helping billions of people get to work, keep their lights on, and heat their homes. Attendees will also learn more about the industry’s digital transformation, which has now been supercharged by the advent of advanced artificial intelligence (AI) programs, often referred to as frontier models. The rise of AI has been anticipated for years, but the widespread excitement, controversy, and debate surrounding its capabilities suggest that we are truly entering a new era of computing and software. Where AI ultimately leads us all remains difficult to predict. What is clear is that the industry’s mission remains unchanged. The business must continue to operate safely, remain resilient in the face of market uncertainty, and responsibly deliver the energy needed to fuel economic progress. New technologies, particularly AI, will play a major role in this effort if they are able to enhance human expertise and help organizations make better decisions. Several industry leaders will share their perspectives on these topics during ATCE’s Opening General Session. Moderated by 2026 SPE President Jennifer Miskimins, the panel will feature Ahmed Alebri, CEO of ADNOC Onshore; Peter Larden, senior vice president of upstream, conventional, and heavy oil for ExxonMobil; Lorenzo Simonelli, chairman and CEO of Baker Hughes; and Ezra Yacob, chairman and CEO of EOG Resources. Additional panels and technical sessions will explore topics including agentic AI, growing energy demand from data centers, and the challenge of improving recovery from unconventional reservoirs as many of the most productive US shale plays continue to mature. One more thing that attendees can expect to find in the SPE Pavilion this year is a special print edition of JPT, produced in partnership with the not-for-profit organization Project InnerSpace. The special issue features original JPT articles and technical paper synopses focused on next-generation geothermal systems. Our goal is to help oil and gas professionals better understand how the industry’s expertise, technologies, and decades of subsurface experience can contribute to the progress being made in this growing field of subsurface engineering. It is an exciting time for the oil and gas industry, but it is not free of major challenges. At ATCE, many of those challenges will be discussed and debated by the engineers, scientists, executives, and technical professionals working to identify practical solutions. I hope many of you will be part of those conversations and help shape the future of our industry when you return to your organizations. As I often do, I would also like to thank the many SPE members and volunteers who have devoted countless hours to organizing ATCE and the SPE’s other events throughout the year. Their efforts help make SPE the industry’s unrivaled forum for advancing petroleum engineering knowledge and sharing technical expertise. Much of that work takes place behind the scenes, but it is deeply appreciated by all of us at JPT. For more information about ATCE 2026 and to register, please visit the conference website.

title: Out-of-Distribution Inverse Design of Elastic Networks with Differentiable Graph Neural Network Molecular Dynamics
abstract: Machine-learning-based inverse design can accelerate the discovery of materials with targeted properties, but conventional structure--property models often require large training datasets and generalize poorly beyond their training distribution. Here, we present a differentiable inverse design framework based on a graph neural network molecular dynamics simulator. By combining a short dynamical initialization with physics-based refinement during simulation, the framework enables optimization well beyond the conditions represented in the training data. Using disordered elastic networks, we show that a simulator trained only on non-auxetic systems with Poisson's ratios between 0.1 and 0.4 can design strongly auxetic networks with values as low as -0.3. The framework also produces stress--strain responses outside the range observed during training, creates localized mechanical defects absent from the training data, and generalizes across system size, enabling optimization of networks tested up to 5000 nodes despite being trained only on networks with fewer than 200 nodes.

title: Episodic Drought Alters Sweetpotato Root System Architecture Attributes During Storage Root Initiation and Early Bulking Stages
abstract: Cumulative evidence from cereal crops and model systems indicates that root system architecture (RSA), including deeper, lower-cost exploratory roots, contributes to drought resilience; however, the role of comparable RSA traits in vegetatively propagated root crops such as sweetpotato remains poorly defined. Two greenhouse experiments characterized RSA responses to episodic drought (EP) events during the establishment and storage root (SR) initiation at 5 to 15 days after planting (DAP) (Expt. 1), and SR attributes at 50 DAP (Expt. 2) in the following three sweetpotato genotypes: ‘Beauregard’ (BX), ‘Evangeline’, and breeding line LA11-88. The experimental treatments were a well-watered control (WWC), a continuous drought control [no water control (NWC)], EP1 (WW-NW-WW), and EP2 (NW-WW-NW). In Expt. 1, the genotypes differed in RSA responses to episodic drought. Under EP1, LA11-88 exhibited 29% and 34% greater main root length than BX and EV, respectively, and maintained more stable lateral root number and lateral root length. In Expt. 2, EP1 reduced storage root count (SRC), storage root length, and storage root diameter in EV and BX, whereas LA11-88 showed only a 20% reduction in SRC relative to WWC. Both NWC and EP2 suppressed SR formation among genotypes. The response of LA11-88 is consistent with evidence from other crops that greater root elongation and RSA plasticity can contribute to drought resilience. The results support the hypothesis that RSA plasticity is associated with sweetpotato response to episodic drought events. These findings identify root system architecture attributes associated with adaptation to episodic drought that may serve as practical phenotyping targets for developing drought-resilient sweetpotato cultivars.

title: Design of an Air Source Heat Pump System with “One Energy for Multiple Uses” and Numerical Simulation of Airflow Field in Solar Greenhouses
abstract: To address the issues of airflow stagnation, uneven temperature and humidity distribution, high risk of disease outbreak, and the urgent demand for energy-saving heating in small- and medium-size solar greenhouses under closed winter operation in cold and arid regions of northern China, we constructed a multienergy complementary system coupling heat copper tube, double-vacuum solar collectors with an air–electric hybrid air source heat pump. Leveraging the operating characteristics of the air source heat pump, the system achieves “one energy for multiple uses,” covering energy storage heating, ventilation cooling, and indoor airflow circulation. In our study, Fluent software was adopted to perform numerical simulations on different air outlet schemes of the exhaust duct, and the optimal pipeline scheme was selected, with air volume uniformity as the evaluation index. A simplified greenhouse model was established to analyze the airflow field distribution characteristics in the crop canopy area. Meanwhile, combined with the heating and air exchange performance of the unit, greenhouse ventilation regulation strategies under different weather conditions were formulated. Our results show that the four-outlet scheme delivers more balanced air volume distribution in the pipeline, and its air supply uniformity better matches the spatial characteristics of the greenhouse. The wind speed at a crop canopy height of 0.2 to 1.0 m inside the greenhouse stabilizes at 0.32 to 0.56 m·s –1 , which can effectively break the air stagnation state and improve the crop growth microenvironment without additional circulating fans. The system can simultaneously realize indoor airflow circulation and moderate cooling while heating and storing energy, reducing greenhouse operation costs and providing a technical reference for energy-saving environmental regulation of small- and medium-size solar greenhouses in northern China.

title: Study on Optimal Uncovering Time of Thermal Insulation Rolling Curtain in Solar Greenhouse Based on Multifactor Coupled Photosynthetic Model
abstract: Uncovering and closing operations of thermal insulation rolling curtains in solar greenhouses in cold and arid regions lacks quantitative standards, and traditional management experience is difficult to adapt to the light-temperature characteristics of double-layer shed structures. Using a solar greenhouse with an inner arch shed for overwintering celery cultivation as the experimental object, we conducted continuous in situ monitoring of CO 2 concentration, air temperature, and light intensity inside the greenhouse in winter. Three classic photosynthetic models—the nonrectangular hyperbola, exponential equation, and modified rectangular hyperbola models—were selected to construct a multifactor integrated photosynthetic model by coupling temperature and CO 2 concentration correction factors. The dynamic changes of crop net photosynthetic rate under different curtain uncovering times were quantitatively simulated to screen the optimal uncovering period of the thermal insulation rolling curtain. The results show that after curtain uncovering in the morning, light radiation intensity is the dominant regulatory factor of net photosynthetic rate, with a significantly higher influence weight than temperature and CO 2 concentration. Under sunny conditions, 8:30 to 9:00 AM is the rapid growth window of net photosynthetic rate, which is the optimal operation interval for uncovering the thermal insulation rolling curtain. Under cloudy conditions, the photosynthetic rate increases gently, and uncovering the curtain at ∼9:30 AM can balance thermal insulation safety and photosynthetic production efficiency. The research results can provide a theoretical basis and technical reference for the refined environmental regulation of solar greenhouses with inner arch sheds in cold and arid regions of northern China in winter.

title: Makhana cum Fish Farming: An Integrated Production System for Livelihood Improvement and Sustainable Aquatic Resource Utilisation
abstract: — Aquaculture is a major contributor to global food and nutritional security, providing high-quality animal protein. However, increasing pressure on land and freshwater resources necessitates production systems that enhance output through efficient utilization of existing resources. Integrated farming provides a pathway to achieve this by combining biologically compatible production components to improve resource-use efficiency, nutrient cycling and overall system productivity. Makhana (Euryale ferox Salisb.) and fish farming represents a promising aquatic integrated production system in which an economically important aquatic crop and fish are produced within the same water body. Makhana provides a nutrient-rich, low-fat food product with increasing commercial value, whereas fish contributes high-quality protein and essential micronutrients, thereby providing complementary nutritional and economic outputs. Integration can utilize spatial and ecological niches within the water body, facilitate nutrient recycling and generate additional fish production and income without requiring separate land and water resources. This approach is particularly relevant for waterlogged and underutilized landscapes where conventional agriculture is constrained. This review evaluates the biological basis, production practices, resource-use efficiency, productivity, economic potential and livelihood significance of makhana – fish farming, highlighting its potential as a sustainable and resource-efficient model for integrated aquatic production.
journal: International Journal of Forest, Animal and Fisheries Research

title: Domain Adaptation of Foundation Language Models for Legal Document Generation: A Systematic Review and Implications for Analogous Regulated Institutional Contexts
abstract: The adaptation of foundation language models for legal document generation has become a relevant problem in Legal Natural Language Processing, particularly because generated texts must preserve factuality, normative coherence, traceability and control over sensitive information. This systematic literature review maps, classifies and critically analyzes primary studies on domain adaptation techniques for foundation language models applied to legal and normative-argumentative document generation. It also examines the implications of the resulting evidence for analogous regulated institutional contexts that share requirements related to reliability, privacy, auditability and institutional control. The review followed guidelines for systematic reviews in Software Engineering and the applicable items of PRISMA 2020. Searches were conducted in Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore and ACM Digital Library, covering studies published from January 2021 to December 2025 and complemented by backward snowballing. From 200 initial records, 32 primary studies were included. The corpus is predominantly concentrated in the legal domain, with only one study directly addressing document production in Public Security. The results show a recurrent use of hybrid adaptation strategies involving parameter-efficient fine-tuning, retrieval-augmented generation and structured inference, although the literature does not establish a universally superior combination. Data engineering is marked by a trade-off between scale and control, with frequent use of semi-synthetic datasets. Traditional Natural Language Processing metrics remain useful as initial indicators, but are insufficient to assess factuality, normative validity and argumentative consistency. Ethical safeguards, privacy controls and bias mitigation metrics remain underdeveloped. The findings indicate that the institutional adoption of foundation language models for legal document generation should be treated as a problem of architecture, evaluation and governance, rather than only textual performance. These conclusions are directly grounded in the Legal NLP literature, while their transfer to analogous regulated institutional contexts should be understood as a functionally motivated implication requiring domain-specific empirical validation.

title: Asset Use Risk Management in the Agro-Industrial Complex: Theoretical and Methodological Foundations and Practical Solutions
abstract: This article examines the asset use risk management process in the agro-industrial complex (AIC) under conditions of increased uncertainty, climate change, and digital transformation. The article explores the nature and classification of risks specific to tangible, intangible, and biological assets in the AIC. Based on a systems-process approach and international standards (ISO 31000, COSO ERM), an adapted risk management model has been developed that takes into account seasonality, biological cycles, technological vulnerability, and regulatory aspects of agricultural production. An algorithm for integrating risk-based management into corporate planning systems, digital platforms for precision farming, and predictive maintenance is proposed. Particular attention is paid to the development of key risk indicators (KRIs), scenario modeling, insurance and hedging instruments, and organizational and managerial mechanisms for implementing a risk culture. The study's results can be used by agricultural holding management, government regulatory agencies, research organizations, and educational institutions when developing sustainable development strategies for the agro-industrial complex.

The Socio-Technical Architecture of Post-Consumer Food Waste: An Empirical Evaluation of Urban Household Dynamics in Nigeria
abstract: Traditional agricultural discourse distinguishes upstream food loss in developing countries from downstream consumer waste in high-income countries. But rapidly urbanizing and changing economic conditions in Sub-Saharan Africa are creating a transitional environment where household food conservation efforts are being undermined by the challenges posed by municipal utility failures and structural bottlenecks. In this study, we have investigated the behavioral factors, socio-demographic patterns, and infrastructural barriers leading to post-consumer food waste in urban Nigerian households. We used a mixed-methods survey to measure sample sizes and used the usual finite population models as Utiya does. The digital distribution network was mostly male (76.1%) and educated (73.6%), and therefore the sample was biased towards the highly educated group of people. The empirical data show that although 66.3% of urban consumers are obsessed with market affordability, purchasing things in bulk to protect against higher food prices, to do so, they often are not able to do things themselves due to system failure. Frequent self-reported planning habits like shopping lists (69.5%) and freezing leftovers (44.2%) are typically negated by power grid failures in urban areas that cause domestic storage spoilage soon after purchase. Moreover, the cross-stage spillover effect was found to be particularly pronounced: 12.6% of consumers can trace household waste back to transit delays and poor road infrastructure that physically hurt and destroy produce before it reaches urban retail centers. These findings indicate that urban food waste in developing regions is not just a matter of consumer choices but a structural problem. The problem of reducing urban solid waste and feeding the people in the region needs to be addressed in a way that supports urban food literacy and public investment in reliable municipal grids and solar-powered cold chains.

title: Spatial and Climate Data Analysis for Machine Learning-based Crop Yield Prediction in Northern Kazakhstan
abstract: Crop yield prediction is important for food security, agricultural planning, and effective resource management, particularly in Northern Kazakhstan, where agricultural production is strongly influenced by climate variability. Changes in temperature and precipitation can affect crop productivity and cause considerable differences in yield between years. The aim of this study is to develop, compare, and evaluate machine learning regression models for wheat yield prediction in the North Kazakhstan Region using climatic data. A dataset covering 1990–2025 was prepared using official crop yield statistics from the Bureau of National Statistics of the Republic of Kazakhstan and climatic data from the NASA POWER database. Daily climatic data were collected from five representative geographical points across the North Kazakhstan Region. The climatic variables included average, minimum, and maximum air temperature and precipitation. Daily temperature values were aggregated into annual mean values, while precipitation was summed to obtain annual totals. The annual values from the five geographical points were then averaged to obtain representative regional indicators. Several regression algorithms were compared, including Linear Regression, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, Bagging Regressor, Decision Tree, and XGBoost. A hybrid model combining XGBoost and Gradient Boosting was also evaluated. Wheat yield was used as the target variable, while climatic variables were used as predictors. To preserve the temporal structure of the data and avoid information leakage, walk-forward validation was applied for 2020–2025. Model performance was evaluated using R², RMSE, and MAE. XGBoost demonstrated the best predictive performance, achieving R² = 0.811, RMSE = 1.436 c/ha, and MAE = 1.160 c/ha. The results demonstrate the potential of machine learning and climatic data for wheat yield prediction and agricultural decision support in Northern Kazakhstan.

title: ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES AND CONSTRAINTS OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ADOPTION IN KAZAKHSTAN’S RESOURCE-ORIENTED ECONOMY
abstract: The article explores the economic opportunities and structural constraints of artificial intelligence adoption in Kazakhstan in a resource-oriented economy where extractive industries are a significant part and the level of high-tech diversification is relatively low. The study seeks to assess the potential macroeconomic impact of AI in several areas and to determine the conditions of its contribution to sustainable economic development. A sectoral analytical framework is used, which involves integrating information from the national accounts with AI productivity coefficients from international empirical research. It examines the main sectors of the economy, such as industry, trade, transport, energy, finance, agriculture and health, as well as the communications industry. Emphasis is placed on new technologies like machine learning, deep learning, large language models, and generative AI, which offer further automation and decision support opportunities for various sectors. Under the adopted assumptions, the model-based scenario estimate suggests that the potential economic impact of AI use in Kazakhstan may range between USD 1.6 and 2.59 billion per year, or around 0.9%–1.5% of GDP. This estimate should be interpreted as an indicative scenario-based result derived from international productivity coefficients and Kazakhstan’s sectoral GDP structure, rather than as a direct empirical measurement of the current level of AI adoption by Kazakhstani enterprises. The most substantial potential effect is concentrated in industry, trade, and transport, whereas the contribution of other sectors is more moderate but remains macroeconomically relevant. At the current stage, AI is mainly considered as a tool for efficiency improvement rather than as a driver of structural transformation. The study also highlights crucial constraints, such as a lack of digital infrastructure, human capital, research and development intensity, and reliance on resource-intensive industries. These all limit the diffusion and multiplier effects of AI technologies. It shows the need for policies that are coordinated with respect to technological modernization, education and economic diversification in order to attain the long-term benefits of AI. If left unchecked, AI can exacerbate existing structural imbalances, instead of helping to transition to a knowledge-based economy.

title: Digital terrain modeling for hydrological analysis and territorial planning in eastern and southeastern regions of Kazakhstan
abstract: The study presents a reproducible methodology for regional digital terrain modeling based on Sentinel-1 SLC radar imagery for Almaty, Zhetysu, Zhambyl, Abai, and East Kazakhstan regions. The objective was to generate a geoinformation terrain layer suitable for hydrological analysis, surface runoff interpretation, identification of flood-prone depressions, morphometric assessment, and territorial planning in areas with contrasting plains, piedmonts, intermontane basins, and mountainous landscapes. The workflow combines interferometric processing in SNAP with subsequent DEM post-processing and spatial analysis in ArcGIS. Sentinel-1 image pairs were selected using temporal interval, orbit identity, relative orbit consistency, baseline length, spatial overlap, and expected coherence. Processing included metadata verification, precise S-1 Back Geocoding, Enhanced Spectral Diversity correction, interferogram and coherence generation, Goldstein phase filtering, phase unwrapping in SNAPHU, geocoding, mosaicking, hydro-correction, and derivation of slope, aspect, hillshade, flow direction, and flow accumulation layers. The resulting DEM and its visual representations reveal clear altitudinal and morphostructural differentiation across the study area. Lowlands, piedmont belts, dissected mountain slopes, watershed divides, talwegs, and valley systems are distinguishable in both color elevation and hillshade outputs. The model provides a practical regional basis for watershed delineation, erosion-control planning, contour organization of agricultural landscapes, assessment of slope processes, and preparation of flood modeling scenarios. The analysis also demonstrates that Sentinel-1 InSAR products should be interpreted as regional analytical terrain models rather than centimeter-level elevation datasets. For local engineering design, flood hazard mapping at fine scale, or microrelief reconstruction, integration with LiDAR, UAV photogrammetry, or ground geodetic measurements remains necessary. This distinction is essential for selecting adequate datasets, defining acceptable accuracy, and avoiding methodological overstatement in applied hydrological and planning studies. The proposed workflow is therefore suitable for regional screening, comparative mapping, and preparation of subsequent detailed field verification in data-limited mountain and piedmont environments.

title: DOES THE DIGITAL ECONOMY INCREASE RURAL HOUSEHOLD INCOME? AN EMPIRICAL STUDY FROM CHINA
abstract: In the era of rapid technological advancement, the digital economy has emerged as a crucial catalyst for socioeconomic transformation. This study comprehensively investigates the impact of the digital economy on rural household income in China, utilizing nationally representative microdata from the 2018 China Family Panel Studies (CFPS). To ensure reliability, we rigorously address potential endogeneity issues through advanced econometric techniques and conduct robustness checks. Baseline empirical results robustly demonstrate that the digital economy significantly increases rural household income. Mechanism analysis reveals that this positive effect is primarily driven by two pathways: facilitating the transition of the rural labor force into non-agricultural employment and substantially enhancing households’ entrepreneurial capabilities. Furthermore, a detailed heterogeneity analysis uncovers several nuanced patterns. First, a notable regional disparity exists; the income-enhancing effects are significantly stronger in the economically advanced eastern regions compared to central and western areas. Second, social capital exhibits a distinctive U-shaped moderating effect, meaning the digital economy’s impact is most pronounced at both extremely high and extremely low levels of social capital. Third, regarding income structure, the digital economy disproportionately benefits non-agricultural income rather than traditional agricultural income. Finally, terrain effects play a critical role; the positive impact is more evident in non-plain regions, which typically suffer from geographical disadvantages and information asymmetry. Ultimately, these findings provide compelling empirical evidence elucidating how the digital economy drives rural income growth, offering valuable insights and targeted policy recommendations for bridging the digital divide in China and other developing countries. Existing literature highlights that the relationship between broadband access and labor market outcomes has been a focal point for researchers and policymakers.

title: 3D models from geological maps: strengths and weaknesses from the Pasubio Massif (Southern Alps)
abstract: 3D geological models provide digital representations of subsurface architecture and are increasingly applied in both academic research and industry. Their construction can follow implicit or explicit approaches, depending on data availability and final modelling applications. While 3D models based on subsurface data are traditionally employed in several fields of study, models derived from outcrop data are increasingly being developed. In this study, newly acquired geological mapping data from the Pasubio Massif (Southern Alps, northern Italy), covering an area of ~36 km² within the geographic extent of the CARG sheet 081 “Rovereto”, were used to develop and test an iterative explicit workflow for 3D geological modelling using Move software. The workflow is based on the construction of a structured grid of geological cross-sections, followed by the interpolation of stratigraphic horizons and fault surfaces through Ordinary Kriging. Field observations indicate that the lithostratigraphic units cropping out in the study area form a gently NW-dipping monoclinal structure, exhibit overall constant thicknesses and are affected by the Schio-Vicenza fault system. Model validation first involved a qualitative comparison between mapped geological boundaries and faults with those obtained from the intersection of the modelled surfaces with the topography (DEM), followed by thickness maps evaluation as an internal consistency check. Where inconsistencies emerged, cross-sections were refined and the model was iteratively updated until geological geometries and thickness trends became consistent with field-mapped evidence. A final quantitative assessment was then performed by analysing thickness deviations from mean unit thicknesses and by measuring the spatial overlap between mapped and model-interpolated geological boundaries and fault traces. Comparison between the preliminary and validated models, supported by thickness deviation statistics, indicates that most residual discrepancies are constrained within ±10–20% of expected thickness values. The results highlight the critical role of iterative validation in ensuring geologically robust 3D models, emphasising common sources of uncertainty in explicit geomodelling workflows. This study provides a methodological framework for producing reliable 3D geological models in data-poor regions, complementing the recently published ISPRA guidelines for the organisation and standardisation of model datasets and supporting future applications in academic research and regional or national geological surveys.

title: Microcredit Participation and Farm Productivity in Pakistan: The Role of Financial Literacy, Digital Finance and Climate Shocks
abstract: Microcredit has long been suggested as an important tool for alleviating the financial constraints faced by small-scale farmers. However, it is also true that it cannot have an impact on farm productivity on its own. This study examines the impact of microcredit participation on farm productivity among smallholder farmers in Pakistan and investigates the moderating roles of financial literacy, digital finance use, and climate shock exposure. Primary data were collected from 384 wheat and cotton farmers in Punjab and Sindh Provinces, the obtained data were analyzed using propensity score matching (PSM) to estimate the causal effects of microcredit, and moderated regression models to identify heterogeneous effects. The findings indicate that microcredit participation is associated with significant increases in crop productivity, with wheat and cotton yields rising by approximately 13% and 16%, respectively. The productivity gains are significantly larger among farmers with higher level of financial literacy and those utilizing digital financial services. In contrast, exposure to climate shocks significantly weakens these benefits, reducing the returns to credit-financed investments and highlighting the vulnerability of agricultural production systems. Overall, the results demonstrate that the effectiveness of microcredit is highly conditional on both farmer capability and environmental risk. By integrating financial literacy, digital finance, and climate vulnerability into the analysis, this study contributes to the growing literature on agricultural finance and rural development. The findings underscore the need for integrated policy approaches that combine credit provision with financial education, digital inclusion, and climate-resilient agricultural practices to achieve sustainable productivity gains among smallholder farmers.
