title: The Role of Agricultural Extension in Enhancing Climate Adaptability and Farmers Adoption of Drought Resistant Technologies and Water Conservation Methods in Nineveh Governorate
abstract: The research measured the role of agricultural the awareness implementation and resilience strategies at the Farmer level in the Nineveh Governorate, republic of Iraq as well as to identify the personal factors influencing farmer’s decisions to adopt and protect water smart agricultural technologies , the research was based on the descriptive analytical approach and an available intentional sample and was selected consisting of 200 farmer’s who represented about 30% of the study represented in the villages of the governorate to collect field data a research questionnaire was designed whose apparent validity was verified and it is stability reached 0.881 according to Cronbach’s alpha and the spss program processed the data statistically through descriptive measures and correlation coefficients person and spearman , the results showed a clear indicative paradox the majority of farmers have moderate to high climate awareness at a rate of 82.5% driven by their field experience of drought productivity of strategic crops such as wheat and barley and despite this 57% of farmers fell into the category of low adoption of water conservation and smart agriculture technologies the study attributed this behavioral gap to the poor efficiency of the guidance support provided 44% of the respondents rated the guidance role as lwo due to its reliance on traditional fields correlation analysis revealed the existence of a strong statistically significant of 0.01 between the adoption of modern technologies and educational level and agricultural income and area of possession at the level of 0.05 while a significant inverse relationship appeared with the age factor ,the study recommends a strategic shift towards didital extension by launching interactions activating the role of opinion leaders from innovative models to create local illustrative models and providing government backed soft agricultural loans to reduce the capital costs of smart irrigation networks.
journal: Kirkuk University Journal For Agricultural Sciences

title: Strategi Pemerintah Desa dalam Meningkatkan Pendapatan Asli Desa
abstract: This community service (PPM) activity aimed to assist the village government of Tapak Gedung, Tebat Karai District, Kepahiang Regency, in formulating and implementing strategic approaches to increase Village Original Income (Pendapatan Asli Desa/PADes). The program used a participatory and educational approach involving village officials, BUMDes management, Village Consultative Body (BPD) members, and community representatives, delivered through lectures, training, and Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) covering local potential mapping, productive asset management, and performance-based budgeting principles (money follow the program and money follow the function). Evaluation was conducted through pre- and post-activity questionnaires and direct interviews. The activity identified agriculture, eco-tourism, and the creative economy as the village's key potential sectors and produced strategic priorities including strengthening BUMDes institutions, diversifying agricultural products, developing partnership-based tourism management, and building agro-tourism that integrates farming, culture, and nature. Ninety percent of participants reported that the material was relevant and applicable to preparing the Medium-Term Village Development Plan (RPJMDes) and the Village Government Work Plan (RKPDes). The activity strengthened village officials' understanding of strategic planning and contributed to the village's fiscal independence through collaborative governance. Limitations included a single implementation cycle, a single-village scope, limited follow-up mentoring, and reliance on self-assessment data. The program offers a replicable participatory model for improving village fiscal independence and a foundation for further applied research on sustainable village economic development.
journal: ASPIRASI : Publikasi Hasil Pengabdian dan Kegiatan Masyarakat

title: Penerapan Climate Smart Agriculture melalui Penguatan Budidaya dan Hilirisasi Hasil Pertanian di Desa Jeruk Kabupaten Boyolali
abstract: Jeruk Village in Selo District, Boyolali Regency, has considerable horticultural potential but faces climate variability, postharvest losses, and commodity price fluctuations. The Climate Smart Agriculture program was implemented with Tani Mulyo I Farmers Group to strengthen adaptive cultivation, increase agricultural product value, and develop group capacity. This article aims to analyze program implementation, reported achievements, and beneficiary satisfaction using a descriptive case-study approach. Data were obtained from the 2026 Climate Smart Agriculture program report, the 2025 Community Satisfaction Index report, activity documentation, and relevant scientific literature. Program activities consisted of a smart greenhouse supported by a 5,000-watt solar power system, adaptive planting management, product processing using a vacuum fryer with a capacity of 35 kilograms per cycle, business-management training, and digital marketing. Program documents reported additional income from processed products of IDR 400,000-1,000,000 per month, utilization of approximately three tons of livestock waste per year, estimated emission reductions of 3.78 tons of CO2 per year, and one new employment opportunity. The implementation aspect obtained the highest score of 94.94, while the impact aspect received the lowest score of 94.26, although all aspects remained in the very good category. These findings indicate that integrating adaptive cultivation, renewable energy, product value addition, and group capacity development has the potential to strengthen the resilience of horticultural farming. Nevertheless, the satisfaction index reflects beneficiary perceptions and cannot be interpreted as direct evidence of changes in productivity, income, or environmental impact. Further evaluation requires verified baseline data, broader respondent coverage, and longitudinal measurement.
journal: ASPIRASI : Publikasi Hasil Pengabdian dan Kegiatan Masyarakat

title: Prediction of Potentially Suitable Areas of Hazelnut (Corylus avellana L.) in Romania Based on Bioclimatic Variables
abstract: The hazelnut (Corylus avellana L.) is widespread throughout Europe, except in the northeastern parts. Due to its exceptional nutritional profile and associated health benefits, it’s recognised as a premier nut crop, ranking fifth among nut crops, based on total harvested area. The objectives of this study were: to identify the bioclimatic variables that influence the distribution of hazelnut in Europe, to predict its current and future habitat suitability in Romania and to evaluate the range dynamics. Annual Mean Temperature (BIO1), Precipitation of Warmest Quarter (BIO18), Temperature and Precipitation Seasonalities (BIO4 and BIO15, respectively) were the bioclimatic variables with the highest relative importance. The present climate conditions indicate that around 11% of the country is suitable for hazelnut, i.e. above the 0.8423 threshold. Based on the levels of suitability, more than a quarter of the country presents excellent habitat suitability (above 0.80) and more than half good habitat suitability (above 0.60). Under SSP5-8.5, for the 2081-2100 period, the suitable area for hazelnut (above the 0.8423 threshold) is predicted to be around 1600 km2 (around 700 km2 of expansion area and around 900 km2 stable area). Based on the levels of suitability, for the same SSP and period, the area with climate conditions corresponding to an excellent habitat suitability (above 0.80) is predicted to be about 15900 km2. Modelling climate-driven shifts in species distribution is crucial for equipping forest managers and policymakers with dependable adaptation frameworks. To improve predictive accuracy for hazelnut, future studies should incorporate additional critical environmental variables.

title: From Farm Data to Market Value: a Systemati̇c Revi̇ew of Preci̇si̇on Agri̇culture Technologi̇es and Data-dri̇ven Marketi̇ng Strategi̇es
abstract: This study examines, at a conceptual level, the potential contributions of the multi-layered data ecosystem generated by precision agriculture technologies to agricultural market strategies, drawing on existing literature. The study adopts a systematic review approach conducted under the guidance of a PRISMA flow diagram, with a staged elimination process narrowing 340 titles to 29 included sources, thereby establishing a transparent methodological foundation. The study's primary theoretical contribution is the Farm Data-to-Market Value Transformation Model (FDMV), which—for the first time in the precision agriculture literature—systematically bridges the technical focus of precision agriculture research with the consumer behaviour focus of marketing scholarship. The model integrates Akerlof's (1970) information asymmetry theory, Verlegh and Steenkamp's (1999) country-of-origin effect findings, Nuttavuthisit and Thøgersen's (2017) trust economy framework, and Kotler and Armstrong's (2016) value-based marketing perspective within a single four-stage conceptual structure, presenting this theoretical synthesis as an original contribution absent from existing precision agriculture literature. Findings indicate that IoT sensors, satellite imaging, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), blockchain-based traceability systems, and decision support tools may exert significant influence on quality-based pricing, market segmentation, supply chain coordination, and consumer trust mechanisms. Assessment with specific reference to Türkiye highlights that structural barriers—including land fragmentation, digital literacy gaps, and the absence of data standardisation—are difficult to overcome without integrated policy intervention, while the country's agro-ecological diversity and geographical indication portfolio constitute a favourable foundation for data-driven market differentiation.
journal: Dynamics in Social Sciences and Humanities

title: A Data-Driven Multi-Sensor Detection for Machine Learning Recommendation on the Volcanic Land
abstract: This study presents the development of an advanced, data-driven control system designed to optimize smart farming practices specifically tailored for volcanic soils. While volcanic environments naturally offer a nutrient-rich baseline—averaging 45 ppm nitrogen, 15 ppm phosphorus, and 30 ppm potassium—which is highly conducive to cultivating vegetable crops like chilies, tomatoes, and carrots, they also present a unique agricultural challenge. The inherent instability and extreme variability of these mineral deposits make traditional, static farming methods inefficient and unpredictable. To address this environmental volatility, the proposed system seamlessly integrates real-time sensor technology, the Internet of Things (IoT), and machine learning to continuously monitor and adjust agricultural inputs. By shifting data computation to a cloud-based infrastructure, the system provides farmers with rapid, easily accessible visual dashboards of soil health. At the core of this predictive model is the K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) algorithm, which dynamically calculates and forecasts precise plant nutrient requirements by analyzing the fluctuating soil conditions. The statistical analysis validates the system's effectiveness, successfully mapping the complex relationship between dynamic volcanic soil nutrient availability and actual plant requirements, with normality test scores ranging from 0.55 to 0.65. The sensor-driven framework demonstrated strong predictive performance, achieving 92.25% classification accuracy, 92.50% precision, 92.25% recall, and an F-1 score of 90.5%. Beyond computational accuracy, the system's practical application delivered substantial environmental and economic benefits through resource conservation. The targeted, data-driven interventions reduced water consumption by 27.5% and significantly decreased the need for supplemental nitrogen (18.2%), phosphorus (22.3%), and potassium (21.8%). Concurrently, these precise nutrient optimizations are projected to drive an impressive 23% increase in overall crop yields. Ultimately, this research lays a strong technological foundation for the widespread deployment of real-time, precision agriculture across Indonesia. To further refine this framework, future research will prioritize exploring dynamic, large-scale data normalization methods to further improve classification accuracy and system adaptability.
journal: JOIV : International Journal on Informatics Visualization

title: Land Degradation and Agricultural Productivity in Burkina Faso: Integrating Soil Erosion Modelling and Economy-Wide Impact Assessment Using a CGE Framework
abstract: Background: Land degradation represents a major environmental and development challenge in Sub-Saharan Africa, where agricultural systems remain highly dependent on natural soil fertility and rain-fed production. Soil erosion and declining land quality reduce ecosystem services and threaten food security, rural livelihoods, and economic stability. Burkina Faso is particularly affected due to high exposure to climatic variability and intensive land use pressure. Objectives: This study aims to assess the impact of land degradation on agricultural productivity in Burkina Faso and to evaluate its economy-wide consequences using an integrated biophysical and computable general equilibrium modelling framework. Methods: The study combines the Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (RUSLE) model with a recursive dynamic computable general equilibrium (CGE) model. The RUSLE model is used to estimate spatial soil erosion and derive land productivity loss coefficients across agricultural regions. These coefficients are then introduced as exogenous productivity shocks into the CGE model calibrated on the 2016 Social Accounting Matrix of Burkina Faso. The CGE framework captures interactions among production sectors, households, government, and external trade. It allows assessment of direct and indirect effects of land degradation on agricultural production, income distribution, and macroeconomic performance under different scenarios. Results: The RUSLE results indicate that approximately 28% of agricultural land in Burkina Faso is affected by degradation, corresponding to an estimated economic loss of 321.34 billion CFA francs. Crop-specific results show that staple crops such as maize, millet, sorghum, and groundnuts are the most affected. CGE simulations demonstrate that land productivity losses lead to significant declines in agricultural output, reduced household income, and contraction in macroeconomic indicators. Under the baseline scenario, GDP declines by approximately 27%, while pessimistic conditions lead to even larger reductions. Rural households are disproportionately affected due to their dependence on agriculture. Results also show strong heterogeneity across crop types and regions, reflecting spatial variation in land degradation intensity. Conclusion: Land degradation significantly constrains agricultural productivity and economic performance in Burkina Faso. Integrated biophysical and CGE modelling highlights the importance of sustainable land management policies to mitigate soil erosion impacts and improve agricultural resilience, food security, and rural welfare.
journal: Trends in Ecological and Indoor Environmental Engineering

title: ҚАЗАҚСТАНДАҒЫ ВЕТЕРИНАРИЯЛЫҚ ТАУАРЛАР МЕН ҚЫЗМЕТТЕР НАРЫҒЫН ДАМЫТУДЫҢ ЗАМАНАУИ ТЕНДЕНЦИЯЛАРЫ
abstract: The aim of this study was to analyze current trends in the development of the veterinary goods and services market in Kazakhstan and to identify the main directions of its further development. The research materials included official statistical data from the Bureau of National Statistics of the Agency for Strategic Planning and Reforms of the Republic of Kazakhstan, regulatory and analytical materials of the Ministry of Agriculture of the Republic of Kazakhstan and its territorial subdivisions, as well as scientific publications on veterinary organization, veterinary entrepreneurship and marketing. The study employed methods of analysis and synthesis of scientific literature, statistical and comparative analysis, a structural approach, and generalization. It was established that the current transformation of the market is determined by several interrelated factors, including the digitalization of veterinary activities, strengthening of preventive veterinary medicine, development of animal and animal-product identification and traceability systems, modernization of veterinary infrastructure, development of domestic veterinary pharmaceutical production, and gradual expansion of the commercial segment of services for companion animals. It was demonstrated that a statistical decrease in the volume of certain types of veterinary services should not be interpreted solely as a decline in demand, since the indicators are affected by changes in financing structures and the organization of service provision. Particular importance for the further development of the market is attached to improving access to veterinary care in rural areas, enhancing digital information systems, developing laboratory diagnostics, improving professional qualifications, and ensuring the quality of veterinary medicines. It is concluded that the veterinary goods and services market in Kazakhstan is undergoing structural transformation, while its development is closely associated with the state of livestock production, food security, and the country's export potential.

title: A Neutrosophic Memory-Integrity Calculus for Contradiction-Preserving Persistent AI Agents
abstract: Persistent AI agents increasingly convert interaction histories into long-lived memory, making memory transformation not retrieval alone—a central reliability problem. NMIC (Neutrosophic Memory-Integrity Calculus) formalizes the integrity of write, merge, consolidation, revision, and retrieval operations over persistent memory. Each proposition is represented through an evidence ledger carrying independent truth, indeterminacy, and falsity degrees together with reliability, provenance, temporal validity, contextual applicability, and inter-evidence dependence. A dependence-normalized hazard aggregation preserves simultaneous support and opposition while making the resulting state invariant to exact evidence duplication. Pure consolidation is governed by five integrity conditions: no support invention, no opposition invention, no manufactured certainty, contradiction retention, and provenance coverage. At retrieval time, visibility is separated from assertability so that relevant contradictory memories remain accessible without being promoted to uncontested facts. Seven propositions establish boundedness, independent-evidence reduction, exact-duplicate invariance, temporal non-inversion, manufactured-certainty detectability, contradiction retention, and provenance closure. A fixed-seed synthetic stress benchmark evaluates five mechanism-level failure modes. NMIC preserves conflict/ignorance separation, yields zero duplicate-inflation error, prevents duplicate-driven decision flips, detects 92.22% of randomized manufactured-certainty transformations at tolerance 0.05 with 100% precision, and resolves the benchmark's bi-temporal queries exactly. The resulting calculus provides an auditable mathematical layer for persistent-memory transformations and can be placed beneath existing vector, graph, or language-model memory architectures.

title: Integrating Metagenomics and Deep Learning for Accurate Microbial Species Differentiation
abstract: Accurate identification of microbial species is important for clinical diagnosis, environmental monitoring, and evaluations in agriculture and biotechnology. Conventional culture- and alignment-based metagenomic methods have several drawbacks, including inadequate reference databases, the cost of digital compilations, and poor resolution of closely related taxa and strains. This review explores how Deep Learning is integrated into metagenomics to overcome these limitations. The four architecture families, namely convolutional neural networks, recurrent/LSTM networks, transformer-based genomic language models, and graph neural networks, can be applied to resolve taxonomic classification, genome-resolved binning, gene prediction and functional annotation, and microbiome-phenotype association. The review also discusses data preprocessing strategies as critical determinants of model performance. Despite notable gains over traditional methods, persistent challenges include reference dependency, limited interpretability, data leakage, domain shift across platforms and environments, and the absence of standardized benchmarks. The review shows that future progress depends on multimodal, reference-free foundation models validated on taxonomically independent datasets to achieve generalizable, interpretable, and biologically robust species differentiation.
journal: Journal of Biomedical Systems and Engineering

title: Leveraging on Artificial Intelligence Technology in Boosting Cassava Production in Nigeria: The Gains and Constraints
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology is reshaping agricultural landscape globally by employing data-driven, efficient, and scalable production methods. Nigeria, as the world’s largest producer of cassava, faces persistent challenges like low yield per hectare, pest infestations, climate variability, and inefficient farming techniques. This study focuses on the potential of AI technology to exploit and enhance the nation’s agricultural potentials and productivity. The study decisively examines the application of AI in cassava production in Nigeria, focusing on its gains and constraints. It adopted ways to addressing the critical challenges like climate variability, scarce access to digital farming techniques, and the need for sustainable practices. Using a descriptive and analytical approach based on secondary data from FAO, NBS, IITA, and recent scholarly publications, the study explores AI-driven technologies such as precision agriculture, machine learning, remote sensing, and automation. Findings from the study reveal that AI technology application in cassava production can significantly improve productivity, optimize resource utilization, and reduce post-harvest losses. However, adoption can be constrained by high costs, poor infrastructure, low digital literacy, and weak policy frameworks. This paper investigates how AI technology can be employed to achieve the mass production of cassava in Nigeria, while critically examining the associated gains or benefits and constraints.
journal: Federal University Gusau Faculty of Education Journal

title: DATA SCIENCE-BASED MODELING FOR ELECTRICITY CONSUMPTION FORECASTING
abstract: Accurate forecasting of electricity consumption is central in modern energy systems for both planning and operational decision making. This research proposes a data science driven methodology for predicting electricity demand and directly compares machine learning with deep learning approaches under identical experimental conditions. Specifically, a tree based model, XGBoost, and a recurrent neural network, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), have been evaluated on the same dataset with consistent data preprocessing, splits, and metrics. Currently, tree based models use explicit temporal feature engineering in order to find nonlinear relationships in structured time dependent data. In contrast, LSTM networks learned the temporal dependencies from sequential load observations directly. The performance evaluation of these models is made by RMSE and MAPE. Accordingly, it follows that LSTM yields the highest forecasting accuracy with the superior capturing of temporal dynamics, while XGBoost offers competitive performance with lower computational complexity. This implies that there are some important context-dependent tradeoffs that exist among model accuracy, interpretability, and efficiency when coming to electricity consumption forecasting.
journal: East-West. Eurasian scientific and methodological journal for master and doctoral students

title: Characteristics of express analysis of the financial condition of agricultural sector enterprises under intensifying digitalization
abstract: The purpose of the study is to provide a theoretical substantiation of express analysis of the financial condition of agricultural sector enterprises under intensifying digitalization, clarify its place within financial diagnostics, and develop an authorial approach to rapid analytical assessment. The object of the study is the process of operational assessment of the financial condition of an agricultural enterprise using a limited but information-sufficient set of financial indicators. The methodological basis combines systemic, structural and analytical, comparative, and ratio-based approaches with grouping, generalization, dynamic analysis, and an authorial scoring method. Express analysis is interpreted as a compact sequence of analytical actions that makes it possible to identify critical changes in liquidity, financial stability, business activity, profitability, and cash-flow adequacy within a short period and then determine whether an in-depth analysis is required. The study substantiates the need to consider seasonality, production-cycle duration, the substantial share of inventories and biological assets, volatility of purchase and selling prices, dependence on natural factors, and uneven cash inflows. Digitalization primarily changes the speed, frequency, and information richness of express analysis because data can be automatically obtained from accounting systems, banking services, warehouse records, and production accounting. Six analytical directions and an authorial integral express-assessment scale from 0 to 100% are proposed. The scale is designed for preliminary diagnostics and does not replace a comprehensive financial analysis. A digitalized express-analysis procedure should combine automatic data collection with analytical verification, comparability across identical phases of the production cycle, control of data quality, and preservation of managerial responsibility for interpreting the results. The practical significance of the proposed approach lies in its potential use by financial managers, executives, and owners of agricultural enterprises for regular identification of risk zones, monitoring changes in key indicators, and timely transition to a deeper analysis of the causes of financial deterioration.
journal: Scientific Notes of Lviv University of Business and Law

title: O‘zbekistonda Oziq-ovqat Xavfsizligini Innovatsion Rivojlantirishning Iqtisodiy Mexanizmlari Va Yo‘nalishlari
abstract: This article examines the economic mechanisms for ensuring food security in Uzbekistan under conditions of innovative development. The study analyzes grain production dynamics during 2020–2025, the production of major food crops, regional differences in agricultural output, and changes in food prices. The role of digitalization, modern agricultural technologies, resource-efficient production, and innovative infrastructure in strengthening food security is substantiated. Based on the findings, recommendations are developed to improve the economic mechanisms of an innovative agri-food system.

title: ЭКОНОМЕТРИЧЕСКОЕ МОДЕЛИРОВАНИЕ И ОЦЕНКА ПОКАЗАТЕЛЕЙ РАЗВИТИЯ ХЛОПКОВО–ТЕКСТИЛЬНЫХ КЛАСТЕРОВ
abstract: The article is devoted to the development and application of an econometric model in the form of a system of simultaneous equations for forecasting the development indicators of a cotton-textile cluster (CTC). Particular attention is paid to testing the identifiability of the system. Due to the presence of endogenous variables, the two-stage least squares method (2SLS) is applied to estimate the model parameters. The authors propose an over identified system consisting of six linear equations with four variables. Based on this model, a six-step algorithm for evaluating CTC development indicators has been developed in specialized econometric software. At the first step, the volume of raw cotton (seed cotton) production on a farm is determined using either a classical linear equation or the Cobb-Douglas production function in logarithmic form. The result of this step is the pure theoretical forecast values of the volume of raw material produced, excluding the influence of random factors. At the second step, the volume of cotton fiber production is calculated: for this purpose, the previously obtained value of the raw cotton volume is multiplied by the technological fiber yield coefficient. From the third to the fifth step, the indicators of the vertically integrated technological chain are calculated, covering enterprises of the oil and fat sector, as well as spinning, weaving, finishing, and garment production. At the sixth step, an algorithm for calculating financial indicators is applied, which makes it possible to assess the overall economic efficiency of the CTC.

title: A Human-Centered Machine Learning Dashboard for Real-Time Smart Farming Decision Support
abstract: The integration of machine learning (ML) into precision agriculture has advanced predictive accuracy for tasks such as crop monitoring, irrigation scheduling, and yield estimation. However, many existing IoT-based smart farming systems remain technically driven, offering limited attention to how farmers and field operators actually interact with and interpret model outputs. This gap often results in low adoption rates, as complex predictions fail to translate into actionable, trustworthy decisions for end users. This study proposes a human-centered machine learning dashboard designed to bridge predictive modeling with real-time, farmer-friendly decision support. The system integrates IoT sensor data streams with ML-based prediction modules, presented through an interactive, usability-tested interface that emphasizes clarity, accessibility, and interpretability over raw technical complexity. A working prototype was developed and evaluated using both quantitative usability metrics (e.g., task completion time, System Usability Scale scores) and qualitative feedback from target users to assess the dashboard's effectiveness in supporting field-level decisions. The proposed system architecture, dashboard interface, and underlying ML pipeline are implemented as open and reproducible source code, enabling replication and adaptation across similar smart farming contexts. Results indicate that the human-centered design significantly improves users' comprehension of model outputs and their confidence in acting on system recommendations, without compromising predictive performance. This research contributes a practical framework for designing machine intelligence systems that prioritize end-user experience alongside technical accuracy, offering implications for the broader development of human-centered AI in agricultural and IoT-driven decision support environments.
journal: Smart Human-centered Emerging Research in Machine Intelligence

title: Reinvestment Ventures as a Pathway to Sustainable Livelihoods for Small-Scale Maize Farmers in Kondoa District, Tanzania
abstract: Small-scale maize farmers often need to make one harvest serve several purposes: food, school costs,farm inputs, and capital for another livelihood activity. This study examined whether reinvestingmaize-sale income in other crops, horticulture, livestock, and small businesses was associated withmore sustainable livelihoods among farmers in four wards of Kondoa District, Tanzania. A crosssectional mixed-methods design combined a household survey of 406 farmers with focus-group andkey-informant evidence collected in 2022. Descriptive statistics established the prevalence ofreinvestment, Cronbach’s alpha assessed the internal consistency of two livelihood-outcome indices,chi-square tests examined ward differences, and ordinary least-squares models with HC3 robuststandard errors estimated adjusted associations. Half of respondents reported using maize income tosupport other crops (50.5%), 45.2% horticulture, 51.0% livestock, and 40.5% a small business. Theasset-improvement and social-well-being indices showed good internal consistency (α=.777 and.815). Crop reinvestment was positively associated with asset improvement (B=.166, p<.001) andsocial well-being (B=.123, p<.001). Livestock (B=.106, p=.005) and small-business reinvestment(B=.092, p=.003) were also associated with social well-being. Among respondents with completeincome data, small-business reinvestment was associated with 40.6% higher income from otherlivelihood activities (B=.341, p=.039), controlling for maize income and household characteristics.Focus-group accounts helped explain these patterns: farmers described diversification as a practicalresponse to unreliable maize markets and as a way to meet everyday household needs. Because theevidence is cross-sectional and self-reported, the findings indicate association rather than causation.Strengthening market access, financial capability, and context-specific advisory services may helpfarmers convert maize earnings into more resilient livelihood portfolios.
journal: The UONGOZI Journal of Management and Development Dynamics

title: Exploring Pathways for Artificial Intelligence Applications in Rural Areas: A New Mechanism for Youth Participation in Rural Revitalization
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being integrated into agricultural production, rural industrial operations, public services, and cultural communication. Its practical value in rural contexts lies in its capacity to process dispersed, repetitive, and time-sensitive information across production, business, and grassroots governance. Image recognition, text processing, knowledge retrieval, and data analysis can enhance record management, anomaly detection, and service responsiveness. This paper examines the practical rationale for AI applications in rural areas, analyzes the conditions enabling youth participation, and delineates the division of responsibilities among young people, farmers, grassroots officials, agricultural technicians, and technology firms. It proposes four application pathways: record-based monitoring and on-site verification in agricultural production; product-information integration and market-feedback analysis in rural industrial operations; knowledge management and feedback mechanisms in rural public services; and community participation and governance in rural culture and tourism. Youth can contribute through needs assessment, technological mediation, digital content management, and organizational coordination. Effective implementation requires reliable data records, clearly defined review responsibilities, sustained technical and organizational support, privacy protection, and equitable benefit-sharing arrangements.

title: Microelement Biogeochemistry in Meadow-Oasis Soils and Legumes of the Fergana Valley
abstract: This study is devoted to the geochemical assessment of the composition and spatial distribution of chemical elements in meadow–oasis soils developed within the alluvial fans of the Isfara and Sokh rivers in the western part of the Fergana Valley, as well as in associated leguminous crops, including Vigna radiata, Phaseolus aureus, and Arachis hypogaea. The vertical distribution patterns of microelements in soil profiles were investigated, and key geochemical regularities of element accumulation were identified. Clarke concentrations and dispersion coefficients were calculated relative to lithospheric and soil background values to evaluate elemental enrichment and depletion. In addition, the distribution of chemical elements within different plant organs was analyzed, and biological absorption coefficients (Cb) were determined. Based on Cb values, absorption activity sequences were established, enabling classification of elements according to their bioaccumulation potential in plant biomass. The results indicate that Mo, Zn, and Ni exhibit the highest biological activity and accumulation capacity, whereas Fe, Cr, and Co demonstrate comparatively low biological uptake.

title: 6G-Enabled Intelligent IoT: Emerging Architectures, AI-Native Networking, Digital Twins, and Security Challenges
abstract: The convergence of sixth-generation (6G) wireless communication, artificial intelligence (AI), edge intelligence, and the Internet of Things (IoT) is transforming the conventional connectivity-oriented IoT paradigm into an intelligent, autonomous, and context-aware cyber-physical infrastructure. Unlike previous generations, 6G is being conceived not merely as a higher-capacity communication system but as an AI-native platform capable of jointly optimizing communication, computation, sensing, control, and intelligence. This evolution is particularly significant for IoT environments, where billions of heterogeneous devices, sensors, actuators, autonomous machines, vehicles, robots, and cyber-physical assets will generate highly dynamic and geographically distributed data. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of 6G-enabled intelligent IoT, emphasizing emerging architectures, AI-native networking, network and system digital twins, distributed intelligence, semantic communications, reconfigurable intelligent surfaces, integrated sensing and communication, and security mechanisms. A multidimensional taxonomy is developed according to communication technologies, intelligence placement, learning paradigms, architectural layers, digital-twin functions, and security mechanisms. The paper critically examines centralized, edge, federated, distributed, and multi-agent intelligence architectures and discusses the roles of deep learning, reinforcement learning, federated learning, generative AI, and explainable AI in autonomous network optimization. Particular attention is devoted to digital twins as closed-loop environments for network monitoring, prediction, experimentation, and control. Security challenges are analyzed across device, edge, radio access, AI-model, digital-twin, orchestration, and application layers, including adversarial machine learning, model poisoning, privacy leakage, identity attacks, zero-day attacks, and supply-chain vulnerabilities. Comparative analyses of technologies, datasets, simulation platforms, and performance indicators are provided. Representative applications in smart manufacturing, intelligent transportation, healthcare, agriculture, energy, robotics, and smart cities are examined, followed by an illustrative case study of an AI-native 6G smart-factory ecosystem. Finally, unresolved challenges involving scalability, synchronization, explainability, energy efficiency, interoperability, security, standardization, and trustworthy autonomy are identified. The paper concludes with a research agenda centered on self-evolving AI-native networks, secure digital-twin ecosystems, semantic intelligence, quantum-resistant security, integrated sensing-computing-communication, and sustainable 6G-IoT infrastructures.
journal: International Journal of Research and Review in Applied Science, Humanities, and Technology

title: Next-Generation Cyber-Physical Systems: Architectures, Intelligent Technologies, Applications, and Future Research Directions
abstract: Cyber-Physical Systems (CPSs) have evolved from tightly coupled sensing, computation, communication, and control platforms into highly distributed intelligent ecosystems in which physical processes, computational resources, communication infrastructures, artificial intelligence, digital twins, and human participants interact continuously. The emergence of edge and fog computing, 5G/6G networks, machine learning, reinforcement learning, federated learning, blockchain, digital twins, autonomous systems, and foundation models is substantially changing the architecture and operational characteristics of next-generation CPSs. Unlike conventional CPS architectures, emerging systems must simultaneously address real-time constraints, heterogeneous data, dynamic environments, distributed intelligence, safety, cybersecurity, privacy, explainability, interoperability, and lifecycle assurance. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of next-generation CPSs from architectural, technological, methodological, application, and research perspectives. A unified taxonomy is developed covering physical, sensing, communication, edge, cloud, intelligence, digital-twin, orchestration, security, and human-interaction layers. The review critically examines centralized, edge-centric, cloud-assisted, distributed, digital-twin-enabled, and AI-native architectures and compares their characteristics with respect to latency, scalability, resilience, computational requirements, interoperability, privacy, and assurance. Mathematical formulations are presented for CPS state estimation, control, resource optimization, anomaly detection, and multi-objective performance assessment. Emerging intelligent methodologies—including deep learning, reinforcement learning, federated learning, graph neural networks, physics-informed learning, generative AI, and foundation models—are analyzed in terms of their applicability and limitations. Applications in smart manufacturing, autonomous transportation, smart grids, healthcare, agriculture, buildings, robotics, and smart cities are discussed, followed by an illustrative industrial CPS case study integrating edge intelligence, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and secure control. Particular attention is given to benchmark datasets, simulation platforms, communication technologies, digital-twin frameworks, and cybersecurity mechanisms. Finally, unresolved challenges concerning real-time AI assurance, semantic interoperability, adversarial robustness, uncertainty quantification, energy efficiency, human autonomy, ethical governance, and verification of learning-enabled controllers are identified. The review concludes by proposing a research agenda toward trustworthy, adaptive, interoperable, and self-evolving CPS ecosystems.

title: Agripreneurship as the New Agricultural Extension Frontier: Incubation, Digital Platforms and Rural Enterprise Development
abstract: Agricultural extension is being asked to solve a problem that conventional technology-transfer models were not designed to address: how to help rural actors convert knowledge, technologies and market opportunities into viable, adaptive enterprises. This critical narrative review examines agripreneurship as a possible new frontier for agricultural extension, with particular attention to business incubation, digital platforms and rural enterprise development. Literature published from 2009 to 27 July 2026 was considered, alongside necessary foundational material, using multidisciplinary scholarly sources and critical appraisal of conceptual, observational, experimental and programme-evaluation evidence. The synthesis indicates that extension has progressively moved towards pluralistic innovation-system roles involving brokerage, network facilitation and capability development, creating an institutional basis for enterprise-oriented advisory work. Incubators and accelerators can add mentoring, finance readiness, legitimacy and network access, but their apparent performance is highly heterogeneous and agriculture-specific evaluations frequently lack credible counterfactuals or long post-graduation follow-up. Digital advisory services more consistently improve information, knowledge and selected practices than final productivity or profit outcomes, while platform models can connect advisory, market and financial functions but also introduce exclusion, dependency, data-governance and bargaining-power risks. Evidence on rural enterprise development is similarly uneven: youth and women can gain skills and opportunity access, yet selection effects, resource constraints and institutional barriers complicate claims that agripreneurship alone generates durable employment or inclusive rural transformation. The review therefore proposes an enterprise innovation-broker model of extension in which technical advice, venture capability, incubation, market and finance intermediation, and digital governance are treated as complementary rather than substitutable functions. The field now requires stronger causal designs, longitudinal venture tracking, distributional metrics and evaluation of hybrid public-private architectures. Agripreneurship is best interpreted not as a replacement for extension, but as an extension frontier whose legitimacy depends on demonstrated additionality, inclusion and public-value accountability.

title: Digital Transformation and Crop Production in Sub-Saharan Africa: Evidence from Dynamic Panel Data Analysis
abstract: Digital transformation can reduce information frictions and expand access to markets, extension services, and financial tools, but its relationship with agricultural outcomes in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) remains sensitive to measurement and econometric specification. This study examines the association between a connectivity-based Digital Transformation Index (DTI) and crop production in 40 SSA countries over 2000-2022 (N = 769 country-year observations). The DTI combines mobile-cellular subscriptions, internet use, and fixed-broadband subscriptions, while the outcome is the natural logarithm of the FAO Crop Production Index (2014-2016 = 100), an aggregate production index rather than an input-normalised productivity measure. Entity fixed effects (FE) provide the main static estimate, while pooled OLS, random effects, two-way FE, System GMM, Difference GMM, component-level models, income-group estimates, and a quadratic specification are used for sensitivity analysis. Entity FE yields a positive DTI coefficient (beta = 0.948, p < 0.001), whereas the estimate is smaller and only marginally significant with year effects (beta = 0.523, p = 0.095). In the dynamic models, System GMM produces a positive but imprecise DTI estimate (beta = 0.031, p = 0.409), while Difference GMM yields a negative and imprecise estimate (beta = -0.059, p = 0.581). Separate income-group FE models show a larger coefficient in low-income countries (beta = 1.841) than in lower-middle- and upper-middle-income groups (approximately 0.48), although no formal cross-group coefficient-equality test is reported. The quadratic FE specification is concave and implies a sample-specific turning point near DTI = 0.709, located in the upper tail of the observed distribution. Overall, the results support a positive long-horizon within-country association in the static FE model, but the weaker time-controlled and dynamic estimates warrant cautious, non-causal interpretation.
journal: Asian Journal of Advances in Agricultural Research

title: Probabilistic Forecasting of Mortality in Kenya Using a Zero-truncated Conway-Maxwell-Poisson Bayesian Generalized Additive Model
abstract: Aims: To develop the Zero-Truncated Conway-Maxwell-Poisson Bayesian Generalized Additive Model (ZTCMP-BGAM) for probabilistic mortality forecasting in Kenya, estimate its parameters, evaluate its performance against three models, and generate probabilistic forecasts of mortality and life expectancy for 2024 to 2053. Study Design: Quantitative secondary data analysis and mathematical modeling. Place and Duration of Study: Kenya, 1950 to 2023 (observation); 2024 to 2053 (forecast horizon). Methodology: UN WPP 2024 graduated death counts and population exposures for Kenya across 101 ages (1950-2023) were used. The ZTCMP-BGAM embeds a zero-truncated Conway-Maxwell-Poisson distribution with an age-specific dispersion parameter within a Bayesian generalized additive model. Parameters were estimated via penalized log-likelihood with a Laplace approximation, implemented in Template Model Builder. The ZTCMP-BGAM was compared against three models in a two-by-two factorial design crossing zero-truncation and flexible dispersion. Performance was evaluated using BIC, in-sample accuracy, an independent dispersion diagnostic, and backtesting over two holdout periods. Forecasts were generated by extrapolating the additive predictor. Results: The ZTCMP-BGAM achieved the lowest BIC (66,003.42). Flexible dispersion accounted for 99,290 log-likelihood units of improvement; zero-truncation contributed 1.5 and 0.36 units within the equidispersion and flexible-dispersion classes, respectively. Departures from equidispersion were confirmed at 96 of 101 ages. Primary backtesting (2014-2023) yielded errors of 19.5% and 29.2% for equidispersion and flexible-dispersion models, respectively; sensitivity backtesting (1994-2023) reversed the ranking (31.8% vs. 24.5%). Life expectancy was projected to rise from 65.94 (95% CI: 65.75-66.15) to 81.23 years (95% CI: 78.87-83.59) by 2053. Conclusion: Flexible age-specific dispersion improves distributional fit; equidispersion is inappropriate across most ages. Out-of-sample forecast performance depends on the mortality dynamics in the holdout period. The framework is transferable to any country relying on UN WPP estimates.
journal: Asian Journal of Probability and Statistics

title: Analyzing the Green Marketing Mix through Social Media in Community-based Agrotourism Development to Support Carrying Capacity: A Case Study in Wates Jaya Tourism Village, West Java
abstract: Tourism growth in Bogor has intensified pressure on established destinations, creating a need for community-based alternatives that can support local livelihoods while respecting environmental carrying capacity. This study examines how the Green Marketing Mix—product, price, place, and promotion—can be integrated with social media in the development of community-based agrotourism in Wates Jaya Tourism Village, West Java. A qualitative case-study approach was used, drawing on in-depth interviews, field observations, source triangulation, SWOT analysis, and the Green Marketing Mix framework. The findings show that Wates Jaya combines natural attractions with agricultural resources, including coffee, mina padi rice-fish farming, Trigona honey, and agricultural-waste utilisation. Green Product strategies can convert these resources into educational tourism experiences, while Green Price can incorporate local welfare and conservation considerations. Green Place positions the village as an alternative to congested tourism areas in Bogor, and Green Promotion uses social media to communicate environmental values and reach relevant visitor segments. However, limited digital literacy, low community participation, internal social tensions, and incomplete agricultural data constrain implementation. The study indicates that stronger community coordination, youth-led digital management, clearer spatial planning, and integrated promotion are important for aligning tourism development with local economic needs and ecological limits. The proposed approach supports agrotourism development without expanding agricultural land into protected areas.

title: Anemia Level Detection and Prediction in Pregnant Women Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning
Smart Farming using Machine Learning: A Review on Recent Trends and Approaches of Crop Yield Prediction
abstract: Crop Yield Prediction (CYP) supports the finest decision‐making to support farmers for crop yields forecasting effectively which can help farmers make precise decisions about planting, harvesting, and development of their crops. However, CYP is a challenging endeavor due to the complexity of the underlying mechanisms and the impact of many variables, such as weather patterns, soil conditions, and crop management practices. Researchers have proposed different CYP models using Machine Learning (ML) techniques on different datasets and experimental settings. However, the reported performance of these models is often not directly comparable due to variations in data sources, spatial and temporal scales, crop types, and evaluation protocols. In this context, this review provides a conceptually integrated and analytical synthesis of CYP approaches. Rather than identifying a universally optimal model, this study highlights that model effectiveness is highly context‐dependent, varying with data modality, agro‐climatic conditions and application requirements. The article also discusses advantages and limitations of different ML models for CYP by a thorough analytical analysis. Besides, it highlights the key challenges for the implementation of ML models for CYP to produce improved crop productivity. This paper has the potential to be a helpful resource for both beginners and experts in the field of agriculture, particularly those who focus on ML‐based CYP and employing different varieties of crops. The outcomes of this review reveal that learning paradigms combined with multi‐source data integration deliver the most reliable yield predictions while also exposing critical gaps in crop diversity, climate coverage, and real‐world expert system deployment. This article is categorized under: Algorithmic Development > Ensemble Methods Technologies > Machine Learning Fundamental Concepts of Data and Knowledge > Explainable AI

title: Energy Harvesting Systems via Peristaltic Micro‐Pumps in Targeted Therapies: Comparative Analysis of Hybrid RSM–ANN Model
abstract: The movement of fluid caused by the contraction and relaxation of flexible conduit walls is known as peristalsis, and it is a phenomenon seen in biological systems such as blood and food flow. In industrial operations, microfluidics, and medicinal applications, understanding heat convection in peristaltic flows is essential. In order to develop medication delivery systems, optimize flow parameters for uniform distribution, and forecast performance under various physiological situations, it is imperative to model heat convection in peristaltic flow. Understanding heat transfer in blood arteries under peristaltic flow aids in temperature regulation in hyperthermia‐based cancer therapies, and artificial neural network models help with real‐time treatment parameter management. This work addresses the peristaltic flow of a Newtonian fluid in a symmetric channel that is governed by three nonlinear coupled partial differential equations. The novelty of the present study lies in combining numerical simulation with response surface methodology and artificial neural networks to analyze and predict pressure rise behavior in peristaltic flow through a porous symmetric channel. This hybrid approach improves prediction accuracy while efficiently capturing the nonlinear characteristics of the flow system. The approximations of long wavelength and low Reynolds number reduce these to nonlinear coupled ordinary differential equations. The solutions obtained using MATLAB's bvp4c routine yield several numerical findings. An empirical relation for is developed using the response surface methodology (RSM) and artificial neural networks (ANNs). The accuracies of the developed empirical relations are verified by calculating the coefficient of determination, , along with an analysis of variance. In this case, high = 98.06% and adjusted = 96.32% values clearly show a good fit of the model. The sensitivity analysis shows that is maximum when the Darcy number, Brinkman number, and Grashof number increase. The primary computation includes mean squared error computation, error histogram generation, and a regression line in the case of ; it results in an MSE of around 1.1839e−09, thereby strongly correlated with the data and model.

Plant-microbe networks under climate change: molecular mechanisms, systems biology, and strategies for ecosystem resilience
abstract: The interplay between plants and their associated microbiomes is a critical determinant of ecosystem resilience under climate change. This review synthesizes current knowledge of plant-microbiome systems, focusing on the molecular mechanisms that govern synergistic interactions and on systems biology approaches to unraveling their complexity. We examine how these networks facilitate plant adaptation to drought, salinity, and extreme temperatures by modulating physiological responses, nutrient acquisition, and defense mechanisms. Multi-omics technologies (metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, metaproteomics, and metabolomics) enable holistic characterization of these interactions, supporting predictive modeling and targeted microbiome engineering. We explore synthetic microbial communities (SynComs) and bioinoculants as innovative solutions to enhance crop resilience and promote sustainable agriculture. Quantitative evidence demonstrates that plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) inoculation under drought stress increases yield by 56% and root biomass by 61% relative to drought-stressed controls, with multi-strain consortia increasing shoot biomass by 70% compared with 28% for single strains, while field trials show approximately 50% reduction in efficacy relative to controlled conditions (22% vs 45% yield increase), highlighting the critical translation gap. Key challenges include inconsistent field performance, formulation stability, commercial viability (> 40% product failure rate), and regulatory fragmentation. Future directions integrating digital twins, AI-driven predictive analytics, and synthetic biology offer important opportunities. This review provides a framework for harnessing plant-microbiome systems to foster climate-resilient agriculture and ensure food security.

An integrated multi-theory SWOT analysis of green internet of things for sustainable digital transformation
abstract: Environmental sustainability faces both benefits and challenges due to the rapid growth of Internet of Things (IoT) technologies. This study proposes an integrated theoretical model for deploying Green Internet of Things (G-IoT) by using a Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats (SWOT) analysis approach and by expanding existing theories from technology adoption, sustainability transitions, and public policy. The study seeks to respond to major gaps in the literature. The study achieves this by providing a systematic approach to understanding the technological, environmental, policy and socio-economic relationships that influence the implementation and outcomes of G-IoT. This study combines expert interviews and detailed case studies to analyse the strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats perspectives. The study reveals important strengths, weaknesses, opportunities arising from policy support and converging technologies and also threats stemming from the digital divide and privacy concerns. A cross-category analysis reveals important dynamics between internal attributes and external influences that ultimately determine sustainability outcomes. The study highlights capabilities of G-IoT to reduce the discord and fragmentation under rising socio-technical divides. However, these depend on strong technological support and steady government funding, while addressing equity and security issues. This study offers policy recommendations and actionable steps for deploying G-IoT within sustainable digital transformations in the urban, industrial, agricultural, and social realms.

From transient shocks to unexpected outcomes: Disruptive drivers in scenario pathways
abstract: Scenario pathways (e.g. for the energy transition) often use a single trajectory or a band. That is not sufficient when one needs to understand why outcomes differ and under what stress or uncertainty they arise. Doing so requires tracking disequilibrium along pathways, comparing runs across"worlds"or storylines, and surfacing outcomes that are unlikely under a central view but plausible when how factors interact is uncertain. Cross-Impact Balance (CIB) is a well-established method for generating pathways. This paper extends CIB to formalise and implement these dimensions in pathway runs, and defines four run types that respectively emphasise one-off shocks, extremes under alternative regimes, influence-structure uncertainty that widens over time, and exogenous shocks as a baseline for comparison. The approach is applied to a socio-technical decarbonisation pathway for illustration. Together, the extensions support stress-testing, comparison across storyline or regime assumptions, and exploration of rare or surprising futures, and help analysts distinguish results that are stable across those assumptions from those that depend on structural uncertainty about the influence table.

title: Synergistic Impact of Spaceborne and Ground‐Based GNSS Observations on Tropical Cyclone Forecasting: A Case Study of Cyclone Kirrily
abstract: Accurate forecasting of tropical cyclones (TCs) is critical for mitigating coastal hazards. Integrating multi‐source observations to improve initial conditions plays a key role in enhancing TC forecast skill in numerical weather prediction (NWP). Although previous studies have demonstrated the value of Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) observations in NWP, the benefits of jointly assimilating spaceborne and ground‐based GNSS observations for TC prediction remains insufficiently explored. This study innovatively implements the synergistic assimilation of spaceborne GNSS radio occultation (RO) refractivity and ground‐based GNSS zenith total delay (ZTD) observations using a regional NWP model and evaluates its impact on the Southern Hemisphere severe TC Kirrily. Data from the Chinese commercial meteorological satellite Tianmu‐1 (TM‐1), the Global Data Assimilation System (GDAS), and Geoscience Australia (GA) are applied. Results show that synergistic assimilation improves the simulated TC structure and surrounding environment, yielding more accurate lower‐to‐middle tropospheric thermodynamic and kinematic forecasts. Verification against ERA5 shows reduced root‐mean‐square errors (RMSEs) for temperature, winds, and moisture, with maximum reductions of 8.1% at 500 hPa, 5.7% at 750 hPa, and 8.0% at 700 hPa, radiosonde verification exhibits a similar pattern. For TC prediction, joint assimilation reduces Kirrily's track errors after 30 hr and improves minimum sea level pressure (MSLP) forecasts, while overestimating maximum surface wind speed (MWS) during early intensification. It also yields a more realistic hydrometeor distribution and enhances rainfall prediction, particularly for light‐to‐moderate precipitation. These findings highlight the potential of exploiting complementary GNSS observations to improve TC forecasting and strengthen early warning capabilities for associated hazards.

title: From Cloud to Pocket: Frontier Edge Foundation Models and the Future of Clinical Informatics
abstract: Objective: To examine the implications for clinical informatics of an inflection in open foundation models designed for on-device and edge deployment, exemplified by the Qwen 3.5 small series (2 March 2026) and Gemma 4 (2 April 2026). Target audience: Clinical informaticians, healthcare chief information officers, hospital governance committees, and natural language processing researchers. Scope: We summarise the technical advances of these releases, situate them within the 2024 to 2026 peer-reviewed evidence on locally deployed clinical large language models, and discuss consequences for privacy, latency, multimodal point-of-care applications, equity, and validation. We argue that for a defined subset of clinical tasks, particularly structured data extraction and template-based documentation, the default of routing all clinical natural language processing through commercial cloud application programming interfaces may no longer be the most defensible choice, while acknowledging that frontier cloud models retain clear advantages for complex clinical reasoning. The field needs reporting standards, governance and liability frameworks, task-appropriate routing mechanisms, and benchmarks tailored to edge deployment.

title: 149. Segmentation guided deep learning for sperm morphology classification in bull breeding soundness examinations.
abstract: Breeding soundness examination (BSE) is one of the most critical management practices to ensure the profitability of a beef herd. Semen analysis of sperm motility and morphology is time-consuming, requires significant training, and is susceptible to human error and subjectivity. The objective of this study was to evaluate the use of computer vision for sperm morphology classification in bulls. We hypothesized that computer vision can accurately perform sperm morphology evaluations compared with human-based classifications. Bos taurus bulls were exposed to BSE following the guidelines of the Society for Theriogenology. Morphology slides were prepared chute-side using eosin-nigrosin staining. Slides were examined using bright-field microscopy at 1000x magnification, and images were captured. Individual sperm cells were annotated using CVAT to segment whole sperm and regions of the sperm (head, midpiece, tail). Individual sperm images were labelled by three trained evaluators as morphologically normal or by location of abnormality. Cell images (n = 473) were used to train a binary baseline convolutional neural network (CNN) model (normal vs. abnormal), and two multi-class CNN models were developed to classify five categories based on defect localization (morphologically normal, head, midpiece, tail, or other defect). The Multiclass Full Image model received the entire segmented sperm as input and predicted the single most biologically relevant defect location. The Multiclass Regional model used anatomical segmentation masks to isolate the head, midpiece, and tail as separate crops, training one independent binary classifier per region, allowing a single cell to receive multiple simultaneous defect classifications. Both models used transfer learning with ImageNet-pretrained backbones, nested cross-validation for hyperparameter selection, and consistent data augmentation and pixel normalization. Performance was assessed using accuracy, macro precision, recall, macro F1-score, and balanced accuracy, with regional model metrics reported independently per anatomical region. The binary baseline model achieved a balanced accuracy of 0.794 and macro F1-score of 0.792, partially distinguishing normal versus abnormal sperm cells. Among the multiclass models, the Multiclass Full Image model reached a balanced accuracy of 0.559 and macro F1-score of 0.537. The Multiclass Regional model improved on the ability to predict defect location with balanced accuracies of 0.664, 0.816, and 0.822 and macro F1-scores of 0.705, 0.831, and 0.841 for head, midpiece, and tail regions, respectively. Within this preliminary dataset, the Multiclass Regional model outperformed the Multiclass Full Image model in predicting primary defect location while retaining the ability to identify concurrent secondary defects, indicating that anatomical region-specific classification better reflected the complexity of sperm morphology abnormalities. While classification by defect location shows promising trends, further improvements are required and will likely depend on increased dataset size and more balanced class representation.

title: 258. Evaluating Insulin Resistance and Sensitivity Values in Beef Steers from Birth to Weaning.
abstract: Although insulin status is known to affect growth and metabolic performance, it is unclear whether maternal insulin status directly affects calf insulin status at birth. Insulin resistance has been evaluated for animal performance in the feedlot but has limited research in pre-weaning calves. Additionally, there has been limited research on how dam insulin resistance relates to calf insulin resistance and performance. The objective of this study was to determine if dam insulin resistance and sensitivity values correspond to offspring insulin resistance and sensitivity values as well as performance characteristics. Steers (n = 43) and their respective dams were evaluated for insulin-related measures at the KSU Agricultural Research Center located in Hays, KS. Dam blood samples were collected after a 12 hour fast, 2 weeks before their expected calving date. Steer blood samples were collected 24 hours post birth. All blood samples were processed to obtain plasma. Individual animal was used for the experimental unit. Weights were collected both at birth (35 ± 4.2 kg) and weaning (183 ± 26.7 kg). Plasma was analyzed for insulin and glucose concentrations with corresponding values utilized to calculate the dam and steer Homeostatic Model Assessment for Insulin Resistance (HOMA-IR; 3.13 ±3.432, 4.90 ±4.077) and Quantitative Insulin Sensitivity Check Index (QUICKI; 0.36 ±0.062, 0.32±0.030) indices. Relationships between variables were assessed with Pearson correlation coefficients in R Studio (R-4.5.1.pkg) Effects were considered significant at P ≤ 0.05 and considered tendency when 0.05 < P ≤ 0.10. Dam QUICKI was positively correlated with steer QUICKI (r = 0.46, P = 0.002) indicating dam insulin sensitivity values may influence calf insulin sensitivity values at birth. Steer QUICKI was negatively correlated with weaning gain (r = -0.60, P < 0.001) indicating steers with lower gain had lower insulin sensitivity. Steer HOMA-IR was positively correlated with weaning gain (r = 0.52, P < 0.001) showing that steers with higher insulin resistance values had higher weaning weight gain. Dam QUICKI was negatively correlated to weaning gain (r = -0.38, P = 0.01) and tended to be negatively correlated with birth weight (r = -0.28, P = 0.07). Both indicating greater maternal insulin sensitivity is related to reduced offspring weaning gain. Dam insulin sensitivity values may be associated with calf insulin sensitivity values at birth, but they are negatively correlated with birth weight and weaning gains. Higher insulin resistance values may be associated with higher weaning gains and birth weight. These dynamics assist in explaining the key endocrine foundation that cattle may carry throughout their production. Further research is needed to determine if dam insulin sensitivity and insulin resistance values are related to steer insulin sensitivity, insulin resistance, and performance later in their production, both in backgrounding and in the feedlot.

title: 73. Award Talk: Machine Learning for Economic Decision Making in Texas Stocker Cattle Operations.
abstract: Stocker operations occupy a pivotal position in the U.S. beef value chain, purchasing weaned calves and developing them on pasture to feeder-ready weights prior to feedlot placement. In Texas, which accounts for approximately 14% of total U.S. cattle and calves, stocker enterprises simultaneously absorb price risk on both the buy and sell side of every production cycle. The U.S. cattle industry contributed approximately $101.1 billion to total U.S. agricultural receipts in 2023, with feeder and stocker transactions representing a core share of that value. Auction prices for stocker and feeder calves at benchmark Southern Plains markets have exhibited dramatic cyclical volatility over the past two decades, ranging from a 25-year low near $103/cwt in 2003 to an all-time record exceeding $462/cwt in late 2025, a nearly 4.5-fold swing driven by interacting cycles of drought-induced herd liquidation, corn and fuel cost shocks, and shifting domestic and export beef demand. Yet buy-sell decisions across stocker enterprises remain largely driven by market intuition rather than data-driven price forecasts. This study addresses that gap by developing and benchmarking a suite of machine learning and time-series forecasting models for stocker calf auction prices in Texas, with explicit integration of both supply-side cost drivers and demand-side market signals. Six forecasting models were evaluated: three time-series models (ARIMA, SARIMA, SARIMAX) and three multivariate machine learning models (RF, AdaBoost, SVR). The target variable was the weekly average stocker calf auction price ($/Cwt) obtained from USDA AMS auction reports spanning 2017-2026. Six exogenous predictors were compiled across two categories. Demand-side proxies included feeder cattle futures prices and the beef retail/wholesale price spread, reflecting buyer willingness-to-pay and downstream consumer demand pull on stocker prices. Supply-side and macroeconomic drivers included corn prices, natural gas prices, the U.S.-Mexico exchange rate, the Consumer Price Index. All series underwent preprocessing including stationarity testing, seasonal decomposition, and feature engineering prior to model fitting. All models were evaluated under a walk-forward validation framework, this approach replicates real-world deployment conditions and preserves temporal ordering. Model performance was assessed using MAE, RMSE, and R2. Walk-forward validation results demonstrated that machine learning models outperformed time-series approaches across all error metrics. Among time-series models, SARIMAX yielded the strongest performance (R2=0.84), with the inclusion of demand-side predictors improving substantially over the SARIMA and ARIMA baselines. AdaBoost achieved the highest overall accuracy (R = 0.93), outperforming RF and SVR, suggesting that the nonlinear interactions among demand-side and supply-cost predictors exceed the capacity of linear time-series structures to capture. Overall, these results underscore the value of integrating demand-side market signals with supply-cost drivers under a walk-forward framework for stocker cattle price risk management in Texas. Future research should explore weight-class segmentation across Texas production zones and incorporation of drought indices as additional supply-demand proxies.
